stepTexts.stir_fry_veg: Add carrot, cabbage, shiitake and kamaboko and toss another 2–3 minutes. Keep the vegetables bright and slightly crisp because they continue cooking in the soup.
stepTexts.simmer_soup: Pour in the prepared soup and bring to a lively simmer. Add bean sprouts and cook about 2 minutes, skimming any foam; the broth should be savoury and full-bodied but not milky.
stepTexts.add_noodles: Add champon noodles directly to the wok and simmer 3–4 minutes, or according to the package, so they absorb the soup. Return the seafood to perfect doneness, divide noodles and toppings between bowls and serve immediately.

recipe_000043.title: Classic Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
recipe_000043.description: A simple everyday Japanese soup where dashi provides umami and miso is dissolved at the end for a fragrant, rounded finish. Tofu and wakame make the classic combination, but the salt level should always be adjusted to the specific miso used.
recipe_000043.animeContext: Inspired by the traditional home-food atmosphere of Demon Slayer. This is a culinary-cultural association rather than a claim about one exact bowl shown in a particular episode.

miso.name: White, awase or red miso paste

stepTexts.rehydrate_wakame: Soak dried wakame in cool or lukewarm water for about 5 minutes until expanded. Drain well and squeeze gently; a small amount grows significantly, so do not over-portion it.
stepTexts.heat_dashi: Bring dashi to a gentle simmer. Taste it plain before seasoning so you know how salty your miso needs to be; different miso brands vary considerably in salt level.
stepTexts.warm_tofu: Lower the heat and add tofu cut into 1–1.5 cm cubes. Warm for about 2 minutes without vigorous boiling, which can break the delicate tofu.
stepTexts.dissolve_miso: Turn off the heat. Put miso in a ladle or fine strainer, loosen it with hot dashi and dissolve it back into the pot. Start with less, taste, then add more if needed; avoiding a hard boil preserves the freshest miso aroma and flavour.
stepTexts.finish: Add drained wakame and sliced scallion. Reheat only gently if necessary, without bringing the soup to a rolling boil, and serve immediately.

recipe_000044.title: Japanese Caramel Purin
recipe_000044.description: A smooth Japanese caramel custard with a firm but trembling set and a glossy bitter-sweet sauce released when unmoulded. Gentle mixing and low-temperature bain-marie cooking prevent bubbles and keep the texture almost glassy.
recipe_000044.animeContext: Inspired by Gintama’s well-known affection for sweets and parfait-style desserts. This purin card is an editorial sweet-tooth association, not an episode-specific claim.

stepTexts.make_caramel: Put caramel sugar and cold water in a small light-coloured saucepan. Heat without stirring until the syrup turns deep amber, swirling the pan gently. Remove from heat and carefully add the hot water away from your face; it will spit. Divide immediately among four ramekins.
stepTexts.warm_milk: Warm milk with custard sugar and vanilla until steaming but not boiling, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Remove from the heat and let it stand a minute so it is hot but not violently scalding.
stepTexts.mix_eggs: Whisk whole eggs and yolk gently just until uniform. Avoid incorporating air: bubbles create holes instead of the smooth, dense texture characteristic of purin.
stepTexts.temper_filter: Pour warm milk slowly into the eggs while stirring continuously. Strain the custard through a fine sieve twice, then skim visible foam. Divide over the set caramel and cover the ramekins loosely with foil.
stepTexts.bain_marie: Place ramekins in a deep tray and add hot water to halfway up their sides. Bake at 150°C for 25–30 minutes. The edges should be set while the centre still gives a gentle unified wobble rather than sloshing.
stepTexts.cool_chill: Remove from the water bath, cool until no longer hot, then refrigerate at least 3 hours. Full chilling lets the custard finish setting and the caramel loosen into a sauce.
stepTexts.unmould: Run a thin knife around the edge, place a plate over the ramekin and invert decisively. If it resists, hold the base in warm water for a few seconds, dry it and try again.

recipe_000045.title: Ebi Fry — Panko-Fried Shrimp
recipe_000045.description: Straight, crisp Japanese fried shrimp with a coarse panko shell and juicy interior. Small cuts release the abdominal tendons so the shrimp fries almost straight, while careful tail drying reduces oil splatter.
recipe_000045.animeContext: Inspired by the school-and-family food atmosphere of My Hero Academia. No exact ebi-fry scene is claimed without direct evidence.

stepTexts.clean_shrimp: Remove the heads and peel the shrimp, leaving the last shell segment and tail attached. Make a shallow cut along the back and remove the dark intestinal vein, then rinse quickly and pat dry.
stepTexts.straighten: Make 3–4 shallow diagonal cuts across the belly without slicing through. Turn the shrimp over and gently press along the back until the muscle fibres relax and the shrimp lies almost straight; do not crush the flesh.
stepTexts.dry_season: Trim the sharp tail tip and scrape or squeeze out trapped water from the tail fins to reduce dangerous splattering. Pat every shrimp very dry, then season lightly with salt and pepper.
stepTexts.bread: Set up flour, beaten egg and panko in separate trays. Coat each shrimp in a thin layer of flour, then egg, then panko, pressing crumbs onto the body while keeping the tail free.
stepTexts.fry: Heat oil to 175–180°C. Fry only 3–4 shrimp at a time so the oil quickly recovers its temperature; cook about 2–3 minutes, turning once, until the panko is deep golden and the shrimp opaque and firm.
stepTexts.drain_serve: Drain upright or on a wire rack so steam escapes from the crust. Serve immediately with shredded cabbage, lemon and tartar sauce or Japanese mayonnaise.

recipe_000046.title: Isobeyaki (Isobe-maki) Mochi
recipe_000046.description: Grilled kirimochi brushed with soy sauce and wrapped in crisp nori, a simple Japanese snack built entirely on texture and umami. It is commonly called Isobeyaki and is also described as Isobe-maki; the mochi should be blistered outside and molten-chewy inside.
recipe_000046.animeContext: Inspired by K-On!’s tea-time snack culture. The culinary preparation is real, but the app does not claim a specific Isobeyaki scene without direct evidence.

stepTexts.make_sauce: Stir soy sauce with the optional sugar until dissolved. A plain soy version is also traditional; use sweetness only if you like the glossy sweet-savoury style.
stepTexts.toast_first_side: Place kirimochi in a dry non-stick pan over medium-low heat and cover. Toast about 5 minutes, checking occasionally, until the lower face is golden and the centre begins to puff.
stepTexts.toast_second_side: Turn the mochi and cook uncovered for about 3 minutes more, until the second face is lightly blistered and the centre is fully soft and stretchy. Remove as soon as it puffs strongly so it does not burst and leak.
stepTexts.coat: While the mochi is piping hot, brush or dip both faces in the soy mixture. Return to the pan for only 20–30 seconds per side if you want the sauce lightly caramelized; watch closely because soy and sugar burn quickly.
stepTexts.wrap_serve: Wrap each mochi immediately with a strip of crisp nori and serve hot. The contrast is best at once: as cooked mochi cools it firms and loses the soft elastic texture.

recipe_000047.title: Sanshoku Soboro Don
recipe_000047.description: A classic tricolour Japanese rice bowl of sweet-savoury ground chicken, tiny soft egg curds and a bright green vegetable stripe. The defining technique is continuous stirring so both chicken and egg become fine, even soboro rather than large pieces.
recipe_000047.animeContext: Inspired by Food Wars!’ focus on technique and presentation. The dish itself is a real Japanese home-cooking and bento staple; the anime connection here is editorial rather than an episode claim.

stepTexts.season_chicken_cold: Put ground chicken, ginger, soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar in a cold saucepan. Break the meat apart thoroughly before turning on the heat; starting cold makes it easier to create the very fine, even crumbs characteristic of soboro.
stepTexts.cook_chicken: Set over medium-low heat and stir constantly with several chopsticks or a whisk-like motion, scraping the bottom and breaking every clump. Cook 6–8 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked, finely crumbled and the liquid has reduced to a moist glaze rather than a puddle.
stepTexts.mix_eggs: Beat eggs with sugar and salt only until homogeneous. Use a clean small saucepan so the yellow colour stays bright.
stepTexts.cook_egg_soboro: Cook eggs over low to medium-low heat, stirring rapidly and continuously with chopsticks. Break up curds as soon as they form and remove from heat while they are still moist, before they become dry rubbery crumbs.
stepTexts.prep_green: Blanch or reheat the peas just until bright green and hot, then drain very well. If using another green vegetable, cut it into small neat pieces so the three-colour pattern remains distinct.
stepTexts.assemble: Divide steaming rice between two bowls. Cover one third with chicken soboro, one third with fine egg soboro and place a narrow green stripe between them. Serve hot, or cool promptly and safely if packing for bento.

recipe_000048.title: Chawanmushi — Savoury Steamed Egg Custard
recipe_000048.description: A delicate Japanese steamed egg custard suspended in dashi with small pieces of chicken, shrimp, mushroom and fish cake. The signature texture is almost silken: a balanced egg-to-dashi ratio, straining and very gentle steam prevent holes and curdling.
recipe_000048.animeContext: Inspired by the careful home-cooking focus of Today's Menu for the Emiya Family. No exact chawanmushi episode is claimed without direct scene evidence.

stepTexts.prep_fillings: Cut chicken and shiitake into small pieces. Quickly blanch or sear the chicken until the exterior is no longer raw, and briefly blanch the shrimp if they are thick; the gentle custard steam should finish, not rescue, large cold raw fillings.
stepTexts.mix_seasoned_dashi: Season lukewarm dashi with usukuchi, mirin and a small pinch of salt. Let it cool to lukewarm or room temperature; hot stock can begin setting the egg before the mixture is strained.
stepTexts.mix_eggs: Break the eggs and stir gently with chopsticks or a whisk without beating air into them. Measure roughly 100 ml egg for two large eggs and use about 250 ml dashi for the classic soft set.
stepTexts.strain_fill: Combine egg and seasoned dashi slowly, then pass through a fine sieve. Divide chicken, shrimp, shiitake and kamaboko between two heatproof cups and pour in the custard to about three-quarters full; pop or skim surface bubbles.
stepTexts.steam: Cover the cups. Steam over high heat for about 2 minutes to heat them, then reduce to very gentle steam for 10–12 minutes. The water should not violently boil around the cups or the custard will turn porous.
stepTexts.check_finish: The surface should be smooth and set while the centre gives a delicate wobble. Insert a thin skewer: clear broth should appear around it, not raw egg. Garnish with mitsuba and serve warm.

recipe_000049.title: Kashiwa Mochi
recipe_000049.description: A Children’s Day wagashi of soft rice cake filled with smooth anko and wrapped in a fragrant kashiwa oak leaf. The leaf is a ceremonial, aromatic wrapper rather than food; using prepared culinary leaves and the correct joshinko flour is essential.
recipe_000049.animeContext: Inspired by Ranma ½’s broad connection to traditional Japanese sweets and comic food scenes. No exact kashiwa-mochi appearance is claimed without direct episode evidence.

stepTexts.prep_leaves_filling: Use only kashiwa leaves sold for culinary wrapping, not leaves gathered outdoors. Rinse prepared or salt-pickled leaves and drain; if your package specifies boiling/soaking, follow it. Divide anko into eight smooth 25 g balls.
stepTexts.mix_dough: Whisk joshinko and sugar together, then add most of the water gradually until the mixture is thick but smooth and ribbon-like. Hold back a little water because different rice flours absorb differently.
stepTexts.cook_mochi: Cover loosely and microwave in short stages, stirring between them, until the dough is fully cooked, opaque-white to slightly translucent and very hot, about 3–4 minutes total depending on microwave power. Follow package guidance if your joshinko behaves differently.
stepTexts.knead: Transfer to a heatproof surface or bowl and knead with a wet spatula, then with damp hands once cool enough, until the dough becomes smoother, shinier and pliable. Do not over-knead until tough.
stepTexts.shape_fill: Divide into eight equal pieces. With damp hands shape each into an oval, flatten it, place one anko ball slightly off-centre and fold into a half-moon, sealing the edges gently without thinning them to tears.
stepTexts.wrap_serve: Wrap each filled mochi in one prepared kashiwa leaf with the decorative side outward. The leaf perfumes and protects the sweet but is not eaten. Serve at room temperature, preferably the same day.

recipe_000050.title: Gintama-style Giant Japanese Fruit Parfait
recipe_000050.description: A towering Japanese kissaten-style parfait layered with ice cream, whipped cream, fruit and crunchy cereal, pushed into an intentionally extravagant anime presentation. Japanese fruit parfait is a real café dessert; the giant scale here is the app’s playful Gintama-inspired variation.
recipe_000050.animeContext: Parfait is a verified recurring Gintama motif around Gintoki’s sweet tooth. A direct platform reference is season 3 episode 40 (overall episode 139), where Gintoki is treated to parfait; the oversized composition here remains an original app interpretation.

stepTexts.chill_glasses: Chill two tall sturdy parfait glasses for at least 5 minutes. A cold glass slows melting and buys time while you build the upper layers.
stepTexts.whip_cream: Whip the cold cream to firm but smooth peaks and transfer to a piping bag. Stop before it becomes grainy; the cream needs enough structure to support fruit and wafers.
stepTexts.prep_fruit: Wash and dry the berries thoroughly. Slice strawberries and banana immediately before assembly and keep a few attractive pieces whole for the top; wet fruit makes the layers slide.
stepTexts.build_base: Add a thin ribbon of sauce to each glass, then a layer of cornflakes or granola. Add a small amount of whipped cream and press a few fruit slices against the glass for visible colour.
stepTexts.layer: Add vanilla and matcha ice cream, alternating with more fruit and whipped cream. Work quickly and keep the ice cream scoops separated by solid ingredients so the structure does not collapse.
stepTexts.finish_serve: Pipe a tall final swirl of cream and decorate with Pocky, wafer, reserved fruit and a cherry. This deliberately oversized anime-style version should be served immediately with a long spoon before the ice cream melts into the crunchy layers.

recipe_000051.title: Shio Ramen — salt-seasoned ramen with chashu and menma
recipe_000051.description: The Shio Ramen enhances a light chicken and dashi broth flavored with sake, salt and sesame oil. The tagliolini are boiled separately and placed in the hot broth with chashu, marinated egg, menma, onion and nori: the speed of the assembly preserves the consistency of the pasta.
recipe_000051.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Naruto. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

sale_marino_fine.name: fine sea salt (or salted kelp)
sale_marino_fine.note: Start with ½ tsp; adjust only after tasting the broth

stepTexts.step_1: In a small saucepan, warm the chicken broth with the dashi powder, cooking sake and salt, stirring until dissolved. Start with only half a teaspoon of fine salt. Taste the broth before serving and adjust sparingly; dashi, chashu and seasonings already contain salt.
stepTexts.step_2: Stir in the sesame oil and keep the broth hot over very low heat without letting it boil.
stepTexts.step_3: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a rolling boil.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook the fresh ramen noodles for about 2 minutes, keeping them firm to the bite.
stepTexts.step_5: Drain the noodles thoroughly, shaking the strainer to remove excess water.
stepTexts.step_6: Pour the hot broth into two ramen bowls.
stepTexts.step_7: Gently place the noodles in the center of each bowl, folding the strands into an even mound.
stepTexts.step_8: Arrange the chashu slices, halved marinated egg, menma and a generous sprinkling of chives alongside the noodles.
stepTexts.step_9: Tuck a sheet of nori against the rim of each bowl and serve immediately while hot.

recipe_000052.title: Kare Pan — crispy fried Japanese curry buns
recipe_000052.description: The Kare Pan contains a thick curry filling in a leavened and breaded wrap in the panko. After a first leavening the dough is divided, stuffed and sealed, then the sandwiches are fried until they get a golden crust and crunchy. The curry must be cold before filling: so the closure remains compact and the panko adheres during frying.
recipe_000052.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Black Butler (Kuroshitsuji), My Hero Academia. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

curry_giapponese_denso_ben_freddo.name: Cold, thick Japanese curry (with potatoes, carrots and minced meat)

stepTexts.step_1: In a large bowl, add flour, sugar and yeast, then add warm milk.
stepTexts.step_2: Knead for 5 minutes, then add salt and softened butter.
stepTexts.step_3: Work the dough until it is smooth and elastic.
stepTexts.step_4: Cover with a cloth and let rise for 1 hour until doubling.
stepTexts.step_5: Divide the leavened dough into 6 equal balls.
stepTexts.step_6: Spread each ball form a disc with a slightly thicker centre and thin edges.
stepTexts.step_7: Put a generous spoonful of cold dense curry in the middle of each disc.
stepTexts.step_8: Close the edges carefully by sealing them well and giving the classic oval shape to ellipses.
stepTexts.step_9: Pass every sandwich first into the beaten egg and then into the panko making it stick evenly.
stepTexts.step_10: Let the sandwiches rest for 15 minutes.
stepTexts.step_12: Fry the Kare Pan 2-3 minutes per side until they become golden and super crispy.
stepTexts.step_13: Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

recipe_000053.title: Ebi Tendon — shrimp and vegetable tempura over rice with tentsuyu sauce
recipe_000053.description: In the Ebi Tendon the hot rice supports shrimps and vegetables in freshly fried tempura. The batter is mixed quickly with frozen water, while the tansuyu sauce of dashi, soy and mirin is prepared separately and added at the time of serving. The contrast arises from the still warm rice and the cold batter; the sauce is distributed without submerging the crust of the tempura.
recipe_000053.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! (Shokugeki no Soma), Mob Psycho 100. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

gamberone_freschi_sgusciati.name: fresh peeled shrimp, tails left on

verdure_a_scelta.name: vegetables of your choice (pumpkin, eggplant or shiso leaves)
verdure_a_scelta.note: For example pumpkin, eggplant and shiso leaves, cut into pieces suitable for tempura.

riso_bianco_per_sushi_o_riso_originario_.name: steamed white rice (sushi rice or another short-grain rice)

stepTexts.step_1: In a saucepan, add the dashi broth, soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
stepTexts.step_2: Brings to a slight boil for 2 minutes so that the sugar melts and the alcohol of the mirin evapori.
stepTexts.step_3: Turn it off and keep it off.
stepTexts.step_4: Practice 3-4 small diagonal cuts on the belly of each shrimp and gently spread it out to prevent it from curling up during cooking.
stepTexts.step_5: Work the yolk slightly with ice water.
stepTexts.step_6: Mix the flour all at once and mix very little with the chopsticks (the batter must remain lumpy and very cold).
stepTexts.step_7: Heats abundant oil at 180°C.
stepTexts.step_8: Slightly infarina shrimps and vegetables, dip them in the cold batter and fry them for about 2-3 minutes until the tempura is golden and crispy.
stepTexts.step_9: Place the hot rice in the bowls (Donburi), sprinkle it with a spoonful of Tentsuyu sauce, stick over the shrimps and vegetables in tempura and add another thread of hot sauce before serving.

recipe_000054.title: Hambagu — Japanese hamburger steak with demi-glace sauce
recipe_000054.description: Hambagu are oval meatballs of mixed minced meat, onion and panko softened in milk. After the roasting they are finished in a pan with lid, while the cooking juices become the base of a tasty sauce to be poured on the portions. The sauce is built in the same pan used for meat, recovering the browning bottom and allowing it to thicken briefly.
recipe_000054.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Spy x Family, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

panko.name: Panko (pangrattato) softened in 2 tablespoons of milk

stepTexts.step_1: In a frying pan brown the chopped onion with a little oil until it becomes golden and soft, let it cool completely.
stepTexts.step_2: In a large bowl, mix the minced meat, the cooled onion, the softened panko in the milk, the egg, salt, pepper and a sprinkle of nutmeg.
stepTexts.step_3: It kneads vigorously by hand for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes compact and slightly sticky.
stepTexts.step_4: Divide the dough into two large oval meatballs.
stepTexts.step_5: Switch the dough from one hand to another to eliminate internal air bubbles.
stepTexts.step_6: Practice a slight pressure in the center of each burger with your thumb (it will prevent it from swelling excessively during cooking).
stepTexts.step_7: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat.
stepTexts.step_8: Cook the hamburgers for 3 minutes per side until golden.
stepTexts.step_9: Add 2 tablespoons of water in the pan, cover immediately with the lid and let steam over low heat for 6-8 minutes.
stepTexts.step_10: Transfer the burgers to the dishes.
stepTexts.step_11: In the same pan with meat juices, combine butter, ketchup, tonkatsu sauce, water and sugar.
stepTexts.step_12: Boil for 2 minutes mixing until you get a shiny and dense sauce.
stepTexts.step_13: Add the hot sauce over the Hambagu and serve with rice or vegetables.

recipe_000055.title: Miso Nikomi Udon — udon noodles simmered in miso broth
recipe_000055.description: Miso Nikomi Udon simmers udon in a rich dashi-and-red-miso broth alongside tender chicken, shiitake mushrooms and tofu. Cook the chicken thoroughly before the noodles go in, then finish each serving with an egg and scallions. For a creamy yolk use only pasteurized eggs; check the chicken's core temperature before serving.
recipe_000055.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Yuru Camp△, Natsume Yuujinchou. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

pasta_di_miso_rosso_o_misto.name: red or mixed miso paste (Aka Miso)

petto_di_pollo_tagliato_a_bocconcini.name: chicken breast cut into small pieces

funghi_shiitake_freschi_incisi_a_croce.name: fresh shiitake mushrooms engraved on a cross

uovo_fresche.name: pasteurized eggs suitable for a soft yolk

stepTexts.step_1: In a pot, in terracotta (Donabe) or in a pot with a thick bottom, add the dashi broth and the mirin.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring the dashi broth to a gentle simmer.
stepTexts.step_3: Take a ladle of hot broth, melt the miso paste inside with a whisk or chopsticks, then add it back into the pot mixing well.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the bite-sized chicken pieces, shiitake mushrooms and tofu cubes to the broth.
stepTexts.step_5: Simmer the chicken pieces over medium heat; 5–7 minutes is only a guide. Check with a food thermometer that the centre reaches at least 74 °C, cooking longer if needed.
stepTexts.step_6: Combine the noodles udon directly in the stewed boiling broth and cook for another 4-5 minutes to absorb the flavors of miso.
stepTexts.step_7: Use pasteurized eggs if you want a creamy yolk. Crack one into the centre of each serving, turn off the heat and cover for about 2 minutes until the whites have set. If the eggs are not pasteurized, cook both whites and yolks thoroughly.
stepTexts.step_8: Garnish with the fresh onion and serve very hot directly from the pot.

recipe_000056.title: Chirashizushi — festive sushi rice topped with fish and vegetables
recipe_000056.description: The Chirashizushi has on the sushi rice seasoned and warmed a mosaic of omelette strips, fish, shrimp, cucumber and salmon eggs. The preparation is above all a delicate assembly; the sea ingredients intended to be served raw require a specific verification of fitness and conservation.
recipe_000056.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Fruits Basket, Kimi ni Todoke. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

riso_per_sushi_cotto_e_condito_con_aceto.name: rice for cooked sushi and seasoned with rice vinegar

uovo.name: egg (to make the thin cottage kinhi tamago)

stepTexts.step_1: Spread the cooled, seasoned sushi rice evenly in a wide serving bowl.
stepTexts.step_2: Beat the two eggs with a pinch of salt and sugar.
stepTexts.step_3: Cook a very thin omelette in a lightly oiled pan; cool and cut into fine strips (kinshi tamago).
stepTexts.step_4: Cover the surface of the rice with the fine omelette strips.
stepTexts.step_5: Arrange the diced salmon, tuna, peeled cooked shrimp and thin cucumber slices attractively on the rice. Use salmon and tuna expressly supplied as suitable for raw consumption, following the supplier's freezing and refrigeration guidance. Keep chilled and assemble just before serving; a fresh appearance does not establish safety.
stepTexts.step_6: Add a little salmon roe (ikura) at the centre; sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and thin nori strips.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve cool, with soy sauce and wasabi on the side.

recipe_000057.title: Kurogoma Dango — toasted black sesame dumplings
recipe_000057.description: The Kurogoma Dango are balls of glutinous rice first boiled and cooled in water and ice, then stuck on skewers and slightly grilled. A hot sauce of black sesame paste, sugar, soy and mirin completes the surface. The light grilling of the skewers precedes the nappatura: the black sesame remains the protagonist of the glossy and fragrant finish.
recipe_000057.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Gintama, Samurai Champloo. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

90ml_di_acqua_tiepida.name: lukewarm water
90ml_di_acqua_tiepida.note: Add it gradually: the actual quantity depends on the absorption of rice flour.

stepTexts.step_1: In a bowl, mix the gluten-free rice flour with sugar.
stepTexts.step_2: Combine the water flush by kneading with your fingers until a soft bread with a consistency similar to the earlobe is formed.
stepTexts.step_3: Divide the dough into 12 equal balls by rolling them between the palms of the hands.
stepTexts.step_4: Dive the balls into a pot of boiling water.
stepTexts.step_5: When they come up, let cook for another 2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_6: Drain immediately and immerse them in a bowl of water and ice to block the cooking and make them elastic.
stepTexts.step_7: In a saucepan, combine black sesame paste, sugar, soy sauce, mirin and water.
stepTexts.step_8: Heat on a sweet heat mixing for 2 minutes until the sauce becomes dark, velvety and fragrant.
stepTexts.step_9: Stick 3 balls of dango on each bamboo skewer.
stepTexts.step_10: Slightly grill the skewers on a non-stick pan for 1 minute per side, then nappa generously with the hot black sesame sauce before serving.

recipe_000058.title: Hanami Dango — three-color spring rice dumplings
recipe_000058.description: The Hanami Dango alternate three balls of glutinous rice and silk tofu in pink, white and green colors. The mixture is divided and colored with strawberry and matcha, then boiled, cooled and stuck on skewers according to the traditional sequence. The green, white and pink sequence on the skewer distinguishes these dangos: they are used at room temperature after cooling in water.
recipe_000058.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer (Kimetsu no Yaiba), Clannad. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

fragola_in_polvere_o_1_goccia_di_coloran.name: strawberry powder or 1 drop of natural pink colour (for pink dang)

stepTexts.step_1: In a bowl, add the glutinous rice flour, sugar and silk tofu.
stepTexts.step_2: Hand knead until the tofu integrates completely creating a homogeneous and soft compound.
stepTexts.step_3: Divide the dough into 3 equal parts (about 80g each).
stepTexts.step_4: Leave the first white part.
stepTexts.step_5: Combine Matcha powder with the second part and knead until it becomes clear green.
stepTexts.step_6: Combine the strawberry powder/coloring to the third part and knead until it becomes pink confection.
stepTexts.step_7: Shape 4 balls from each cake of color (you will get 4 green balls, 4 white and 4 pink).
stepTexts.step_8: Bake the balls in boiling water divided by color (first white, then pink, finally green) for about 2-3 minutes since they come up to the surface.
stepTexts.step_9: Transfer them to frozen water.
stepTexts.step_10: Stick a green ball down on each bamboo skewer, a white ball in the middle and a pink ball on top.

recipe_000059.title: Asari no Sakamushi — sake-steamed clams with ginger
recipe_000059.description: Asari no Sakamushi steams purged clams briefly with sake, garlic and ginger in a covered pan. The clams open over high heat after the butter has been gently infused with the aromatics; discard any that remain closed. Finish the cooking juices off the heat with the remaining butter and a little soy sauce, then serve with fresh chives.
recipe_000059.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! (Shokugeki no Soma), Midnight Diner (Shinya Shokudo). These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Wash the clams thoroughly, already flushed under cold running water.
stepTexts.step_2: In a large pan with lid, dissolve half of the butter and add the sliced garlic and grated ginger.
stepTexts.step_3: Brown on a soft heat for 1 minute.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the clams in the pan and add the Japanese sake immediately.
stepTexts.step_5: Cover immediately with the lid and raise the flame on a live fire.
stepTexts.step_6: Cook for 3-4 minutes by shaking the pan every now and then until all clams open completely (discard those that remain closed). Use live clams from a reliable supplier. Discard broken shells and clams that do not close when tapped before cooking; discard any clams that remain closed after thorough cooking.
stepTexts.step_7: Turn off the heat, add the remaining butter and a thread of soy sauce.
stepTexts.step_8: Mix gently to create a tasty and shiny broth.
stepTexts.step_9: Dust with plenty of fresh chives and serve hot with its broth.

recipe_000060.title: Castella — fluffy Japanese sponge cake
recipe_000060.description: The Castella is a high and soft dessert that gets volume by assembling eggs and sugar for a long time. It incorporates honey and flour sifted without disassembling the mixture, then cooks in the rectangular mold and lets rest wrapped to stabilize the crumb. The rest wrapped after cooking helps to retain moisture; the final veiling of honey completes the golden surface.
recipe_000060.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Si alza il vento (Studio Ghibli), Gintama. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

farina_per_pane_o_farina_00_setacciata.name: flour for bread or Italian 00 flour sieved

stepTexts.step_1: In a cup melt the honey in warm water with the mirin.
stepTexts.step_2: In a large bowl, mount the eggs with sugar using electric whips for at least 10-12 minutes.
stepTexts.step_3: As long as the compound becomes clear, foamy and triple in volume.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the honey mixture in the eggs mounted flush and mix at a low speed for 1 minute.
stepTexts.step_5: Slice the flour on the mixture in three shots, gently incorporating it from the bottom upwards with a spatula to not disassemble the dough.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the dough in a rectangular mold lined with baking paper.
stepTexts.step_7: Cook in the oven at 160°C in a static oven preheated for 35-40 minutes until the surface is golden and a toothpick comes out dry, freshly baked.
stepTexts.step_8: Brush the surface with a veil of honey, wrap the cake in the transparent film and let it rest in the fridge for a few hours: this passage will make the Castle incredibly humid, soft and fragrant.

recipe_000061.title: Sapporo Miso Ramen
recipe_000061.description: The Miso Ramen of Sapporo starts from a base of garlic, ginger, meat and miso red and white slightly toasted. The broth is added gradually; the noodles are cooked separately and the bowl is completed with jumped buds, corn, egg and a nut of butter.
recipe_000061.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! - Shokugeki no Soma, Ramen Daisuki Koizumi-san. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: In a large pot, heat the sesame oil and brown the chopped garlic, grated ginger and the ground pork meat on medium heat until the meat becomes golden and grated.
stepTexts.step_2: Combine sake and sugar.
stepTexts.step_3: Then it incorporates the red miso and the white miso vigorously amalgamating with a wooden spoon to to slightly toast the miso without burning it.
stepTexts.step_4: Slowly add the hot chicken broth, mixing well to completely dissolve the miso.
stepTexts.step_5: Boil over a sweet heat for 10-15 minutes to mix all flavors.
stepTexts.step_6: In a separate pan, skip the soy sprouts with a drop of sesame oil for 2 minutes while keeping them crispy.
stepTexts.step_7: Cook the fresh noodles in boiling water in plenty of boiling water, not salted, following the instructions of the package (about 2-3 minutes), then drain them thoroughly.
stepTexts.step_8: On the basis of each large bowl add the boiling broth with miso and meat.
stepTexts.step_9: Combine the drained noodles by making them stick in the center.
stepTexts.step_10: Place on one side the soy sprouts, the sweet corn, half a marinated egg, a nut of fresh malga butter in the center (typical of the tradition of Sapporo), a sprinkled onion and a sheet of Nori algae stuck on the edge of the bowl.

recipe_000062.title: Kurogoma Nabe — black sesame pork hotpot
recipe_000062.description: The Kurogoma Nabe combines slices of pork, Chinese cabbage, tofu and mushrooms in a single pot. The black miso and sesame sauce is mixed with dash and poured on the ingredients, then it is cooked covered as long as vegetables and meat are ready. Meat and vegetables cook in the same covered pot, to be served hot when the vegetables are tender but not unpacked.
recipe_000062.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Yuru Camp△, Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

fette_sottili_di_pancia_di_maiale.name: thin slices of pork belly (or linza)

cavolo_cinese.name: Chinese cabbage (Hakusai) cut into 4 cm pieces

tofu_setoso_o_fermo.name: silky or firm tofu (cut into cubes)

stepTexts.step_1: Clean vegetables and mushrooms.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the Chinese cabbage into medium-sized pieces and the Shiitake mushrooms by making a cross incision on the chapel.
stepTexts.step_3: In a bowl, melt the black sesame paste with miso, mirin and soy sauce, adding a ladle of hot dashi broth until you get a fluid and homogeneous mixture.
stepTexts.step_4: In a pot, of terracotta (or large saucepan), it radiates the leaves of Chinese cabbage, tofu, Enoki mushrooms and Shiitakes.
stepTexts.step_5: In the middle place the slices of pork belly rolled slightly.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the remaining Dashi broth and black sesame mixture over the ingredients.
stepTexts.step_7: Cover with the lid and bring to a boil over medium heat.
stepTexts.step_8: Continue cooking for about 10-12 minutes until the meat is completely cooked and the vegetables are not tender but fragrant.
stepTexts.step_9: Serve directly on the table keeping the pot warm!

recipe_000063.title: Tenshinhan — crab omelet over rice with sweet-and-sour sauce
recipe_000063.description: Tenshinhan combines a soft omelet with crab or surimi with a bowl of hot white rice. An ankake sauce of broth, soy and condiments, thickened with starch, is poured on the omelette only at the end of cooking. The omelet must remain soft on the surface: the hot ankake sauce is poured only after placing it on the rice.
recipe_000063.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Dragon Ball, Food Wars! - Shokugeki no Soma. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

amido_di_mais_sciolto_in_2_cucchiai_d_ac.name: corn starch dissolved in 2 tablespoons of water

stepTexts.step_1: In a saucepan, add chicken broth, soy sauce, sugar, rice vinegar and oyster sauce.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring to light boiling over medium heat, then add the melted cornstarch and mix continuously until you get a shiny sauce, thickened and velvety, keep warm.
stepTexts.step_3: In a bowl, work the 4 eggs slightly with a pinch of salt, pepper, sesame oil, frayed crab pulp and half of the onions.
stepTexts.step_4: Warm up a large amount of oil in a non-stick pan over a lively heat.
stepTexts.step_5: Add half of the egg mixture for each portion.
stepTexts.step_6: Continue cooking for 1 minute by moving the pan so that the base is represented but the top remains incredibly creamy and soft.
stepTexts.step_7: Place the golden omelet over a mountain of hot rice placed in the middle of a bottom dish.
stepTexts.step_8: Plenty nappa the omelet with the Ankake sweet and sour sauce well warm and garnish with the remaining onions.

recipe_000064.title: Menchi Katsu — crispy minced-meat cutlets
recipe_000064.description: The Menchi Katsu are oval cutlets of ground meat and onion, tied with egg and breadcrumbs softened in milk. After the double breadcrumbs are fried until gilding and served with fresh cabbage and tonkatsu sauce, verifying the internal cooking of the meat. The breading must be gilded evenly, while the meat must be well cooked even in the middle before serving with cabbage.
recipe_000064.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Isekai Shokudo - Restaurant to Another World, Persona 5. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: In a small pan brown the chopped onion with a drop of oil until it becomes transparent and golden, let cool completely.
stepTexts.step_2: In a large bowl, add minced meat, cold onion, egg, breadcrumbs softened in milk, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
stepTexts.step_3: It kneads vigorously by hand until the mixture becomes sticky and homogeneous.
stepTexts.step_4: Divide the dough into 4 oval portions.
stepTexts.step_5: Pass the meat from one hand to another by gently slamming it to eliminate any internal air bubbles that would break the cutlet during cooking.
stepTexts.step_6: Pass each schnitzel first into the flour, then into the beaten egg and finally cover it generously with Panko pressing lightly with your fingers to make the crumbs stick well.
stepTexts.step_7: Heats plenty of oil to fry at 170°C.
stepTexts.step_8: Fry the Menchi Katsu for 5-6 minutes per side on medium-low heat until the crust is dark and golden and the inside is well cooked and juicy.
stepTexts.step_9: Drain on absorbent paper and serve hot accompanied by fresh cabbage and Tonkatsu sauce.

recipe_000065.title: Shogayaki — ginger-glazed pork loin
recipe_000065.description: In the Shogayaki the thin slices of pork are floured slightly, browned in a pan and coated with a sauce based on ginger, soy, mirin and sake. The seasoning is reduced in a few moments until frosting the meat, to be served with finely cut cabbage. The ginger enters the sauce before the reduction in the pan; fresh cabbage and warm rice accompany the frosted slices.
recipe_000065.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Cooking Papa, Food Wars! - Shokugeki no Soma. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

fettine_sottili_di_lombata_o_pancia_di_m.name: thin slices of loin or pork belly

stepTexts.step_1: In a small bowl mix the grated ginger with its juice, soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until it completely melts.
stepTexts.step_2: Spread the slices of pork on a cutting board and dust them slightly with a veil of flour on both sides (this will allow the sauce to thicken and adhere perfectly to the meat).
stepTexts.step_3: Heat a spoonful of seed oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook the pork slices for about 1.5 to 2 minutes per side until they are golden.
stepTexts.step_5: Add the ginger sauce directly above the meat in the hot pan.
stepTexts.step_6: Boil for 1 minute by stirring the pan until the sauce is reduced to a shiny and fragrant frosting.
stepTexts.step_7: Set up the pig side by side with an abundant mountain of fresh hooded cabbage and mayonnaise Kewpie, serving it with bowls of warm white rice.

recipe_000066.title: Mabo Nasu — stir-fried eggplant with miso and minced meat
recipe_000066.description: Mabo Nasu combines browned eggplant sticks and ground pork meat in an aromatic sauce of garlic, ginger, miso and soy. The eggplants return to the pan at the end; the starch thickens the bottom before serving with rice. The eggplants are gathered at the seasoning after the gilding and the corn starch thickens the sauce before the addition of the onion.
recipe_000066.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! - Shokugeki no Soma, Cooking Master Boy. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

melanzana_perline_o_giapponesi.name: Eggplant beads or Japanese beads (cut into 5 cm sticks)

pasta_di_miso.name: miso paste (or Doubanjiang for spicy version)

amido_di_mais_sciolto_in_poca_acqua.name: corn starch dissolved in little water

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the eggplant into sticks and brown in a pan with 2 tablespoons of seed oil over medium heat for 5-6 minutes until golden and soft.
stepTexts.step_2: Remove them and save them.
stepTexts.step_3: In the same pan, add garlic, ginger and minced meat.
stepTexts.step_4: It browns the meat until it changes color and releases its juices.
stepTexts.step_5: Combine miso, soy sauce, sake and sugar by mixing for 1 minute.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the chicken broth and bring it back to a boil.
stepTexts.step_7: Combine the golden eggplant in the pan, mix gently to absorb the flavors for 2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_8: Then add the melted cornstarch together until you get a thick and enveloping sauce.
stepTexts.step_9: Dust with fresh onion and bring on the table a bowl of hot rice.

recipe_000067.title: Monjayaki — Tokyo-style griddled savory pancake
recipe_000067.description: The Monjayaki is prepared on a plate with cabbage, tenkasu and meat or seafood arranged in a ring. In the middle is poured a very liquid batter made of dash, flour and Worcestershire sauce, then the whole is laid out and let form a crust to be collected with small spatula.
recipe_000067.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by K-On!, March Comes in Like a Lion. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: In a jug add Dashi broth, flour and Worcestershire sauce and whisk well.
stepTexts.step_2: The batter will be much more liquid than that of Okonomiyaki.
stepTexts.step_3: Add cabbage, sea meat/fruits and Tenkasu on an electric plate or large hot frying pan.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook by skipping the ingredients for 3 minutes.
stepTexts.step_5: Using two small spatulas, shape the cabbage on the hot griddle into a wide ring or volcano, leaving a hollow in the centre.
stepTexts.step_6: Gently add the liquid batter to the center of the volcano in two shots, allowing it to thicken slightly before mixing all together.
stepTexts.step_7: Spread the mixture on the plate.
stepTexts.step_8: Continue cooking until the lower part creates a dark and crunchy crust.
stepTexts.step_9: You eat directly from the plate with small metal spatula (Hagashi)!

recipe_000068.title: Custard Cream Dorayaki — Japanese pancakes with pastry cream
recipe_000068.description: These Dorayaki replace l'anko with a vanilla custard cream. The cream is thickened and cooled, while a honey batter forms small disks in a pan that are joined to sandwich only after cooling. The small pancakes should be allowed to cool before adding the cream, to preserve the soft filling between the two discs.
recipe_000068.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Doraemon, Kimi no Na wa (Your Name). These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

3_cucchiai_d_acqua.name: water
3_cucchiai_d_acqua.note: Add it gradually to adjust the fluidity of the batter.

stepTexts.step_1: Work the egg yolks with sugar and cornstarch.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat the milk with vanilla without boiling, then add it flush on the egg yolks mixing.
stepTexts.step_3: Put it back on the fire and let it thicken over low heat by always mixing.
stepTexts.step_4: Cool covered with contact film.
stepTexts.step_5: Work the eggs with sugar and honey until they become clear.
stepTexts.step_6: Melt the yeast in the water and add it to the eggs.
stepTexts.step_7: Slice the flour and incorporate it gently.
stepTexts.step_8: Place the dough in the fridge for 15 minutes.
stepTexts.step_9: Heat a non-stick pan slightly greased with oil and clean with absorbent paper.

recipe_000069.title: Baked Yuzu Cheesecake
recipe_000069.description: The Yuzu Cheesecake has a base of cookies and butter and a scented cheese filling with juice and yuzu peel. After cooking in the oven it must cool and rest in the refrigerator to adjust the consistency before cutting. The cheesecake must cool before resting in the refrigerator: the centre is slightly flickering and stabilizes without excessive cooking.

recipe_000070.title: Sakura Mochi — sweet rice cakes wrapped in salted cherry leaves
recipe_000070.description: Sakura Mochi contains an anko ball in a wrap of pink glutinous rice. After cooking and shaping, each sweet is wrapped in a cherry leaf preserved in brine, which offers aromatic and savory contrast. The anko is wrapped in rice molded with wet hands, while the cherry-salted leaf completes the aromatic contrast.

recipe_000071.title: Tantanmen — spicy sesame ramen with minced meat
recipe_000071.description: The Tantanmen combines noodles with sesame and miso broth and a garnish of spicy pork minced meat. The aromatic base is prepared in a pan; the hot broth and pasta meet in the bowl just before adding the meat. The sesame paste melts in the broth directly in the bowls, before adding noodles and spicy meat with bokchoy.

stepTexts.step_10: Garnish in the center with a generous spoonful of spicy meat, the boiled bok choy leaves and a sprinkle of chopped fresh onion.

recipe_000072.title: Classic Griddled Yakisoba
recipe_000072.description: The classic Yakisoba is prepared by jumping precooked noodles with pork, cabbage and vegetables on the plate. The Worcestershire sauce and condiments wrap the pasta in the wok; aonori, red ginger and katsuobushi complete the dish at the service. Stir-frying over high heat helps the sauce coat the noodles; finish with aonori, beni shoga (pickled red ginger) and katsuobushi as garnishes.

stepTexts.step_10: Serve hot garning with Aonori, Beni Shoga and Katsuobushi bows.

recipe_000073.title: Pork Kakuni — soy- and ginger-braised pork belly
recipe_000073.description: Pork Kakuni begins with large cubes of pork belly simmered in water with ginger and the green tops of spring onions. The meat is then braised slowly in sake, mirin, soy sauce and sugar until tender and richly seasoned. Shelled hard-boiled eggs are warmed in the braising liquid towards the end; serve them with the pork, reduced sauce and a little karashi mustard.
recipe_000073.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the pork belly into large cubes from about 4-5 cm.

stepTexts.step_3: Simmer gently for 45 minutes to remove some of the excess fat.
stepTexts.step_4: Drain it and rinse it under warm water.
stepTexts.step_5: In the clean pot add 400ml of water, Sake, Mirin, soy sauce and sugar, bring to a boil.

stepTexts.step_8: Place the tender pork cubes and the egg cut in half in the bottom plates, nappa with the bottom of the cooking and accompany with a pinch of mustard Karashi.

recipe_000074.title: Traditional Winter Oden
recipe_000074.description: Oden is a winter dish of daikon, konnyaku, hard-boiled eggs and fish cakes gently simmered in dashi seasoned with light soy sauce and mirin. Blanch the daikon and konnyaku first, then simmer the main ingredients without a vigorous boil. Add the mochi-filled kinchaku pouches for the final ten minutes and serve with hot broth and karashi mustard.

recipe_000075.title: Katsu Curry Udon — udon noodles with curry and breaded cutlet
recipe_000075.description: The Katsu Curry Udon combines thick udon in a Japanese curry sauce and a crunchy tonkatsu cutlet. The pasta is cooked while the curry and onion base is heated; the cutlet is placed on the bowl only at the time of service. The curry broth remains fluid enough to wrap the udon, while the tonkatsu is resting on only at the end.

recipe_000076.title: Agedashi Tofu — fried tofu in dashi broth
recipe_000076.description: The Agedashi Tofu starts from well-drained and dried tofu cubes, covered with a veil of starch and fried to form a light crust. The tofu is immersed in a dishi broth seasoned and garnished with grated daikons and fresh aromas. The broth pours around the tofu already fried without covering it, to keep the crust distinct from the central soft part.
recipe_000076.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer (Kimetsu no Yaiba), Spirited Away. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Wrap the tofu pan in kitchen paper and rest on a weight for 15 minutes to remove excess water.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut it to 4 or 6 large cubes.

stepTexts.step_4: Turn it off and keep it warm.
stepTexts.step_5: Pass each cube of tofu into the cornstarch by sticking it evenly on all sides.
stepTexts.step_6: Fry in hot oil at 180°C for 3-4 minutes until the outer crust becomes white and crispy.
stepTexts.step_7: Place hot fried tofu cubes in individual bowls.

stepTexts.step_9: Garnish the top of each cube with a grated Daikon bow, a pinch of ginger, onion and Katsuobushi flakes.

recipe_000077.title: Unadon — grilled kabayaki eel over rice
recipe_000077.description: Unadon combines grilled and glazed kabayaki eel with sweet-salad sauce with warm white rice. The condiment of soy, mirin, sake and sugar is squeezed separately and brushed on the eel before placing it on the bowl. The eel is placed on the rice already seasoned and finished with other sauce, then with a pinch of sansho.

recipe_000078.title: Ebi Chili — spicy tomato-ginger shrimp
recipe_000078.description: The Ebi Chili are shrimps slightly covered with starch and white, salted in a spicy tomato sauce with ginger and garlic. The cooking is short to preserve a firm consistency; the dish is served immediately with white rice. The shrimps return to the pan only after the spicy sauce thickens, so they are coated without prolonging the cooking.

recipe_000079.title: Kani Cream Korokke — creamy crab croquettes
recipe_000079.description: The Kani Cream Korokke contains a creamy filling of crab, onion and béchamel in a crispy panic. The mixture is cooled before forming the croquettes; after frying they serve hot with tonkatsu sauce. The creamy heart of crab contrasts with golden breading: after frying the croquettes drain and serve with tonkatsu.

stepTexts.step_9: Drain and agial on absorbent paper.

recipe_000080.title: Sanma no Shioyaki — grilled Pacific saury with daikon
recipe_000080.description: The Sanma no Shioyaki is a whole fish salted and grilled until the skin becomes golden. It is accompanied with grated daikons and essential condiments to leave in evidence the flavor of the fish; the Italian name of the species requires a taxonomic verification. The grated daikon, the soy sauce and the lemon accompany the whole fish, whose skin is made golden on the grill.

recipe_000081.title: Tamago Sando — fluffy Japanese egg sandwich
recipe_000081.description: Tamago Sando is a Japanese sandwich made with soft crustless shokupan, hard-boiled eggs and Kewpie mayonnaise. Mash most of the eggs with mayonnaise, milk and seasonings into a spreadable filling; place half an egg in the centre to create a decorative cross-section. Butter the bread lightly, fill and wrap the sandwiches, let them rest briefly, then slice. The bread is not baked.

recipe_000082.title: Mizutaki Nabe — Hakata-style chicken and vegetable hotpot
recipe_000082.description: The Mizutaki Nabe is a soup in which over thighs and wings of chicken cook in the broth before the addition of vegetables. recipe_000083.title: Tsukemen — dipping ramen with concentrated broth
recipe_000083.description: Tsukemen serves thick noodles separately from a rich, concentrated pork-and-chicken dipping broth seasoned with soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, chilli oil and katsuobushi. Rinse the cooked noodles in cold water to remove surface starch, then arrange them with chashu, a halved marinated egg and nori. Dip each bite of cold noodles into the hot broth just before eating.

stepTexts.step_1: Simmer the pork-and-chicken broth in a small saucepan until reduced, concentrated and deeply savoury.
stepTexts.step_2: Stir in soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, chilli oil and katsuobushi powder to give the dipping broth a rich umami flavour.
stepTexts.step_3: Cook the thick noodles in plenty of boiling water according to the packet instructions, usually about 5–6 minutes.

recipe_000084.title: Chicken Namban — Japanese fried chicken with tartar sauce
recipe_000084.description: Chicken Namban combines breaded and fried chicken treats with a sweet and sour sauce and a Japanese egg tartara. recipe_000085.title: Warabi Mochi — translucent sweets with kinako and kuromitsu
recipe_000085.description: Warabi Mochi is a sweet with a gelatinous consistency obtained by heating water, sugar and starch until they become translucent. After cooling it is cut into cubes and completed with toasted kinako and kuromitsu syrup. The hot mass is cooled in frozen water and divided into cubes, which receive kinako and kuromitsu only after being drained.
recipe_000085.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Samurai Champloo. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_2: Put the saucepan on medium-low heat and mix continuously with a silicone spatula.

recipe_000086.title: Japanese Soufflé Pancakes — tall and fluffy pancakes
recipe_000086.description: The Japanese Soufflé Pancakes owe their height to the gently incorporated mounted egg whites at the base of egg yolks, milk and flour. The batter is slowly cooked in a pan, often covered, and served immediately to maintain the volume. The covered cooking, with small additions of water, allows pancakes to grow in height without losing the soft consistency.
recipe_000086.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Kaguya-sama: Love is War. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: In a bowl, work the egg yolks with milk and vanilla.
stepTexts.step_2: Sift the flour and yeast and add them to the egg yolks mixing until a smooth batter is obtained.
stepTexts.step_3: In a very clean bowl, mount the egg whites with the electric whips, adding sugar in three shots until you get a shiny and stable meringue, with firm but not dry peaks.
stepTexts.step_4: Embed 1/3 of the meringue into the egg yolks batter with the spatula to soften it.
stepTexts.step_5: Then add the rest of the meringue by gently amalgamating from the bottom upwards so that the mixture is not disassembled.
stepTexts.step_6: Grease a non-stick pan with a little butter over very low heat.
stepTexts.step_7: Create high batter hills.
stepTexts.step_8: Add 1 teaspoon of water to the bottom of the pan and cover immediately with a high lid.
stepTexts.step_9: Cook for 5-6 minutes on minimum heat.
stepTexts.step_10: Add a second layer of batter over the pancakes, cover and cook another 2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_11: Gently turn the pancakes, add another teaspoon of water, cover and cook for another 5 minutes.
stepTexts.step_12: Serve immediately hot and soft sprinkled with icing sugar and maple syrup.

recipe_000087.title: Mont Blanc Chestnut Cake
recipe_000087.description: Mont Blanc with chestnuts has a base of Spanish bread or meringue, whipped cream and a cream of chestnuts distributed in decorative threads. The assembly takes place cold to obtain the typical dome shape, completed with icing sugar. The chestnut cream is extruded in thin threads on the cream dome; icing sugar and chestnut complete the decoration.
recipe_000087.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, K-On!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

dischi_di_pan_di_spagna_o_meringhe_tonde.name: ready-made spanish or round meringue discs

castagne_sciroppate.name: chestnuts in syrup (Kuri no Kanrooni) for the top

stepTexts.step_1: In a bowl, work the chestnut cream with soft butter and rum with the electric whip until it becomes velvety and free of lumps.
stepTexts.step_2: Pass it through a fine sieve to ensure fluidity in cream spaghetti.
stepTexts.step_3: Place the sponge bread or meringue discs on the saucers.
stepTexts.step_4: Place in the center of each disc a whole chestnut in syrup.
stepTexts.step_5: Cover the chestnut by creating a mountain / high cupola of whipped cream using a spatula.
stepTexts.step_6: Insert the chestnut cream into a sac-à-poche with a multi-hole nozzle (mouth for Mont Blanc/spaghetti).
stepTexts.step_7: Squeeze the chestnut cream all around the whipped cream dome creating overlapping threads to cover it entirely.
stepTexts.step_8: Dust the top with icing sugar to simulate the snow and lay a chestnut in syrup on top.

recipe_000088.title: Fruit Sando — fresh fruit and whipped cream sandwiches
recipe_000088.description: Fruit Sando pairs soft shokupan bread with whipped cream, sugar, vanilla and fresh fruit. Arrange the fruit along the intended cutting diagonal on the cream-covered slices, then fill any gaps with more cream. Close, wrap and chill the sandwiches before slicing along the diagonal to reveal the fruit pattern. This is a chilled sandwich, not a baked dessert.
recipe_000088.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Cardcaptor Sakura, Horimiya. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

panna_fresca_liquida_da_montare_freddiss.name: fresh liquid cream to be mounted very cold

mandarini_o_uva_senza_semi.name: Cherries or grapes without seeds
mandarini_o_uva_senza_semi.note: Choose one of the two fruits according to the season.

stepTexts.step_1: Mount the cold cream with sugar and vanilla until it becomes firm and structured.
stepTexts.step_2: Spread a generous layer of whipped cream on two slices of bread.
stepTexts.step_3: Arrange the fresh fruit on the cream along the diagonal where you plan to slice the sandwich.
stepTexts.step_4: Position the strawberries so that the cut reveals their characteristic heart-shaped cross-section.
stepTexts.step_5: Cover the empty spaces between the fruit with other whipped cream so as not to leave any air gaps.
stepTexts.step_6: Close with the other slices of bread.
stepTexts.step_7: Wrap the sandwiches tightly in the transparent film and mark the diagonal cut line with a marker.
stepTexts.step_8: Leave in the fridge for 20 minutes.
stepTexts.step_9: Cut in half with a sharp knife following the line to show the fruit design.

recipe_000089.title: Botamochi / Ohagi — glutinous rice sweets with anko
recipe_000089.description: The Botamochi, also called Ohagi, combines glutinous rice and Japanese rice in hand-modeled bites. The anko red bean paste is distributed around or inside the rice, and the sweets serve at room temperature. The anko is flattened on film before wrapping the rice, so each botamochi keeps the rice filling in the middle.
recipe_000089.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Fruits Basket. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

farina_kinako_o_semi_di_sesamo_neri_tost.name: Kinako flour or toasted black sesame seeds (optional for variants)

stepTexts.step_1: Wash the glutinous rice and the normal rice together until the water becomes clear.
stepTexts.step_2: Cook in a rice cooker or a saucepan with 280 ml of water; if using a saucepan, simmer for 15 minutes from the boil.
stepTexts.step_3: Leave to rest covered for 10 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: With a wooden pestle (Kine) or a spoon, it crushes the hot rice in the pot until the grains are partially discarded and the mixture becomes sticky and compact (without reducing it completely to mashed potatoes).
stepTexts.step_5: Divide rice into 6 oval portions with moist hands.
stepTexts.step_6: Take a portion of Anko red bean jam (about 40g), flatten it on the palm of your hand protected by transparent film.
stepTexts.step_7: Place the rice oval in the middle of Anko's dough and wrap the Anko all around the rice by helping you with the film until it is completely covered.
stepTexts.step_8: Serve at room temperature.

recipe_000090.title: Classic Shoyu Ramen
recipe_000090.description: The Shoyu Ramen uses a soy sauce and mirin to flavor a light chicken or dashi broth. The noodles boil separately and the bowl is completed with chashu, ajitama, narutomaki, onion and nori. The altar flavors the broth in the bowls, then the noodles cooked separately are quickly completed with chashu and ajitama.
recipe_000090.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Naruto, Ramen Daisuki Koizumi-san. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

brodo_dashi_o_brodo_di_pollo_leggero.name: Dashi broth or light chicken broth

uovo_marinato_ajitsuke_tamago_a_meta.name: marinated egg Ajitsuke Tamago in half

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the altar: in a saucepan heats soy sauce, mirin, ginger and garlic for 3 minutes over low heat, then filter.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat the chicken broth or dashi until lightly boil and keep it ready without making it reduce excessively.
stepTexts.step_3: Prepare the topping before the noodles: slice the chashu, cut in half the jitama, chop the onion and portion narutomaki and nori.
stepTexts.step_4: Pour the tarare on the bottom of two preheated ramen bowls and add the boiling broth, stirring to evenly distribute the seasoning.
stepTexts.step_5: Cook the fresh noodles in plenty of boiling water for about 2 minutes or for the time indicated by the manufacturer; drain them carefully without rinsing them.
stepTexts.step_6: Transfer the noodles into the broth immediately and separate them with the chopsticks so that they do not remain packed.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with chashu, half ajitama, narutomaki, onion and nori; serve immediately while noodles and broth are still very hot.

recipe_000091.title: Takikomi Gohan — seasoned rice cooked with vegetables
recipe_000091.description: The Takikomi Gohan cooks Japanese rice directly together with dashi broth, chicken and vegetables. The ingredients are placed over the rice before cooking and incorporated only after rest, in order not to compromise the absorption of the liquid. Covered pot rest redistributes moisture in rice; only after the grains are melted without crushing the condiments.
recipe_000091.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Demon Slayer. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

aburaage.name: aburaage (fried tofu browse) cut into strips

stepTexts.step_1: Rinse rice in several waters until the water becomes almost clear, then drain for 15 minutes: rest prevents the bottom from becoming sticky during cooking.
stepTexts.step_2: Slice the rehydrated shiitakes, the carrot and l'aburaage; cut the chicken into uniform dice of about 1,5 cm.
stepTexts.step_3: Pour the rice into the pot or cooker and add dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sake, respecting the level of liquid provided for rice.
stepTexts.step_4: Distribute chicken, shiitake, carrot and aburaage on top without mixing: the ingredients will steam while the rice absorbs the seasoning.
stepTexts.step_5: Brings to a light boil, covers, lowers to a minimum and cook for about 15 minutes without lifting the lid; in cooking use the normal cycle.
stepTexts.step_6: Turn off and let stand covered for 10 minutes, so the moisture is redistributed and the grains finish cooking.
stepTexts.step_7: It stretches from the bottom upwards with a spatula, gently incorporating the condiments without crushing the rice, and hot servants.

recipe_000092.title: Moyashi Itame — stir-fried bean sprouts
recipe_000092.description: In Moyashi Itame the soy sprouts are quickly jumped into the wok with bacon, carrot and onion. Cooking on a lively heat keeps the buds crispy; soy, pepper and sesame oil complete the seasoning. The shoots jumped briefly over high heat to keep biting, and sesame oil enters the finish over off heat.
recipe_000092.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Gintama, One-Punch Man. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Wash the soy sprouts in cold water, drain them very well and dry them: they must enter the pan almost dry to remain crunchy.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the pancetta, carrot and spring onion into thin pieces. Keep the soy sauce, granulated dashi, pepper and sesame oil beside the wok.
stepTexts.step_3: Heat the wok over high heat and brown the bacon without other fats until it releases part of its fat and gets color.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the carrot and stir-fry it for about 1 minute over high heat.
stepTexts.step_5: Add the sprouts and spring onion and stir-fry vigorously for about 2 minutes. The sprouts should soften slightly but remain crisp.
stepTexts.step_6: Season with soy sauce and dashi, mix for a few seconds and turn off before water is formed on the bottom.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with black pepper and sesame oil and serve immediately.

recipe_000093.title: Cheesy Katsudon — breaded cutlet and cheese rice bowl
recipe_000093.description: This Katsu Donburi puts on hot rice a tonkatsu schnitzel with onion and dishi sauce, then complete it with melted cheese. The final cooking must heat the schnitzel without overly soaking the breading. The cheese melts over the cutlet while the egg remains soft; everything is transferred on the rice without breaking the layers.
recipe_000093.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Yuri!!! on ICE. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

cotolette_di_maiale_tonkatsu_gia_pronte_.name: Tonkatsu pork cutlets already ready and sliced

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare two bowls with the rice warm and keep the tonkatsu cutlets already cooked and cut into strips about 2 cm wide.
stepTexts.step_2: In a donburi sauce it simmers dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar; add the onion and cook 3-4 minutes until it becomes translucent.
stepTexts.step_3: Arrange over the onion a sliced cutlet without submerging it completely, so the breading absorbs flavor but does not dissolve.
stepTexts.step_4: Just beat an egg leaving visible egg white and yolk and pour about two thirds around and over the cutlet.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute half of the cheese, cover and cook 60-90 seconds; add the remaining egg and turn off when it is still soft and shiny.
stepTexts.step_6: Carefully slide the contents of the pan onto the hot rice without breaking the schooner.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with residual cheese or chives and serve immediately, before the egg loses creaminess.

recipe_000094.title: Ishikari Nabe — Hokkaido-style salmon hotpot
recipe_000094.description: The Ishikari Nabe is a salmon pot and vegetables in dishi broth seasoned with miso. The fish is added after the plant base to respect the times; a nut of butter at the end of cooking rounds the flavor of the broth. The salmon is added to the final part so as not to break off, and the butter melts in the broth just before the service.
recipe_000094.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Yuru Camp△, Golden Kamuy. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Check the salmon by removing any bones and cut it into bites; prepare potato, carrot, cabbage, tofu and mushrooms in pieces of similar size.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring the dashi to a light boil in the donabe or in a large saucepan and melt the miso in a bowl with a ladle of hot broth, then put it back in the pot.
stepTexts.step_3: Add potato and carrot and cook to simmer for about 8-10 minutes until they begin to soften.
stepTexts.step_4: Combine cabbage, tofu and mushrooms and continue for 3-4 minutes.
stepTexts.step_5: Place the salmon on the surface and cook 6-8 more minutes gently, without boiling violently so as not to break it.
stepTexts.step_6: Taste the broth and correct with a little miso dissolved apart if needed; avoid boiling for a long time after the addition of miso.
stepTexts.step_7: Turn off, add the butter to the center and serve the hot nabe directly from the pot.

recipe_000095.title: Yuzu Shio Ramen — citrus-scented salt ramen
recipe_000095.description: Yuzu Shio Ramen scents a light chicken broth with salt and fresh yuzu zest. Noodles are boiled separately and served immediately with chicken, menma, egg and grated zest, avoiding leaving the dough waiting in the liquid. The fresh yuzu peel is added to the last: it keeps the citrus scent while the noodles are served without waiting.
recipe_000095.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Ramen Daisuki Koizumi-san, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

succo_di_yuzu_fresco_2_scorza_grattugiat.name: grated zest
succo_di_yuzu_fresco_2_scorza_grattugiat.note: to be incorporated into the broth; the final fresh peel remains a separate seal

guarnizioni_fettine_di_petto_di_pollo_co.name: chicken chest cooked at low temperature

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare in advance chicken, menma, egg stew and yuzu peel; bring to a boil a separate pot of water for noodles.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat the filtered chicken broth with salt and sake until a slight bite and taste: it must be clear, savoury but not aggressive.
stepTexts.step_3: Turn off the heat and incorporate yuzu juice and sesame oil only to the last, to preserve the citrus aromas.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook the noodles in boiling water according to the thickness, draining them when they are still elastic; shake them well to eliminate excess water.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute noodles in preheated bowls and pour the yuzu broth immediately.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the chicken, menma bamboo shoots and half an egg, leaving some of the noodles visible.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with freshly grated yuzu peel and serve immediately, before the noodles continue to absorb broth.

recipe_000096.title: Asari Clam Chowder — creamy clam soup
recipe_000096.description: The Asari Clam Chowder is a creamy soup with clams open to steam, potatoes and onion. The clam liquid is filtered and recovered to season the base; the molluscs enter only at the end, without unnecessarily prolonging the cooking. The filtered liquid of clams enters the creamy base with milk and cream; the open molluscs are added at the end.
recipe_000096.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

vongole_asari.name: fresh asary clams (or veracious clams) and purged clams

stepTexts.step_1: Open the clams in a pan with sake and a lid on fire. Before cooking, discard clams with broken shells and live clams that do not close when tapped; after cooking discard any that remain closed. Refrigerate the strained liquid if not using it immediately.
stepTexts.step_2: Separate the clams from the filtered broth and keep everything aside.
stepTexts.step_3: In a pot, melt the butter and brown the bacon with onion, carrot and potato for 5 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Dust with flour and mix well for 1 minute to toast.
stepTexts.step_5: Gradually add the liquid of the filtered clams, the milk and the cream and continue to mix until you reach a velvety consistency.
stepTexts.step_6: Cook for 12 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
stepTexts.step_7: Combine the clams open last, black pepper rule and bring to the diner accompanied by bread croutons.

recipe_000097.title: Kakiage Tempura — crisp vegetable fritters
recipe_000097.description: Kakiage Tempura collects onion, carrot and, optionally, shrimps in small pancakes with irregular surface. A cold batter binds just the ingredients; the frying must be light and crisp, to be served immediately with tentsuyu. Bunches of battery vegetables fry in small quantities; the tempura is drained on the grill and served still hot.
recipe_000097.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Demon Slayer. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Slice onion and carrot very thin and cut shrimp into small pieces; dry everything well and dust with a spoonful of flour.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring the oil to about 170°C in a deep pot and prepare a drizzling grill next door.
stepTexts.step_3: Beat the yolk into the frozen water and incorporate the flour with a few stirs: the batter must remain cold and slightly lumpy.
stepTexts.step_4: Pour only the amount of batter needed to bind vegetables and shrimps, without turning the mixture into a heavy dough.
stepTexts.step_5: Shape small piles on a skimmer or between two spoons and slide gently into the oil.
stepTexts.step_6: Fry a few kakiage at a time for 2-3 minutes per side, turning them once, until they are golden and light.
stepTexts.step_7: Drain on grill, room immediately and serve hot with tentsuyu or salt to the matcha.

recipe_000098.title: Chicken Teriyaki Don — teriyaki chicken rice bowl
recipe_000098.description: Chicken Teriyaki Don combines white rice and browned chicken over thighs from the side of the skin. Soy sauce and mirin are reduced around the meat until it forms an icing, then the chicken is sliced and placed on the rice. The sauce teriyaki shrinks in a pan until the chicken is frosted, which is sliced on the rice and completed with sesame.
recipe_000098.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Cooking Papa, My Hero Academia. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

sovracosce_di_pollo_disossate_con_la_pel.name: bone-in chicken over thighs with skin

stepTexts.step_1: Bucherella the chicken skin with a fork and brown it in a pan over medium heat starting from the side with the skin, without adding fat.
stepTexts.step_2: Cook for 6-7 minutes until the skin becomes golden and crispy, then turn the chicken and let cook for another 4 minutes.
stepTexts.step_3: Remove excess fat from the pan with cooking paper.
stepTexts.step_4: Mix the ingredients of the sauce teriyaki and add it to the pan with chicken.
stepTexts.step_5: Boil the sauce until it becomes shiny and frosted, constantly napping the chicken.
stepTexts.step_6: Cut the chicken into strips, place it on the hot rice, add the caramel sauce on top and complete with sesame and onion.

recipe_000099.title: Anko Dango with Kinako — rice dumplings with sweet bean paste
recipe_000099.description: The Anko Dango are balls of glutinous rice boiled, cooled and sticked on skewers. They are completed with a smooth anko cover and a dusting of sweet toasted toasted toasted kinako flour. Boiled dangos are stopped in frozen water before being infiltrated: anko and kinako are distributed just before the service.
recipe_000099.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Samurai Champloo, Naruto. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

farina_di_soia_tostata.name: toasted soya floura (kinako) mixed with 1 teaspoon sugar

stepTexts.step_1: Pour the rice flour into a bowl and add the water little at a time, kneading until the mass is smooth and soft, similar to the ear lobe.
stepTexts.step_2: Divide the dough into 12 equal portions and form compact balls without cracks.
stepTexts.step_3: Bring to a boil an abundant pot of water and dive the dangos without overloading it.
stepTexts.step_4: When the balls go up to the surface, continue cooking for another 2 minutes to cook well the center.
stepTexts.step_5: Transfer them immediately into water and ice to stop cooking; drain them and dry them gently.
stepTexts.step_6: Throw three dangos for each skewer and distribute over the smooth anko.
stepTexts.step_7: Mix kinako and sugar, dust the skewers just before serving and consume them daily to keep them soft.

recipe_000100.title: Classic Japanese Curry Udon
recipe_000100.description: Japanese Curry Udon serves thick udon in a dashi broth thickened with Japanese curry roux. Onion and meat cook in the tasty base, while noodles are boiled separately before receiving warm curry. The udon boil in separate water, so the warm curry can cover them without becoming too dense in the bowl.
recipe_000100.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Persona 5, Mob Psycho 100. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

fettine_sottili_di_maiale_o_manzo.name: thin slices of pork or beef

stepTexts.step_1: Slice the onion and cut the meat into thin, bite-sized pieces. Bring a separate pot of water to the boil for the udon noodles.
stepTexts.step_2: Meat rosola and onion in casserole for about 3 minutes, until the meat changes color and the onion begins to soften.
