stepTexts.step_3: Add the dashi, soy sauce and mirin; simmer gently for 3–4 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Turn off the heat, incorporate the curry roux little by little until it is completely melted, then rekindle over low heat.
stepTexts.step_5: Cook another 5 minutes stirring: the broth must veil the spoon but remain fluid enough to wrap the udon.
stepTexts.step_6: Cook the udon noodles in the separate pot of water, drain thoroughly and divide among the bowls.
stepTexts.step_7: Pour the boiling curry on the udon, complete with onion and serve immediately.

recipe_000101.title: Yaki Onigiri — grilled rice balls with soy sauce and butter
recipe_000101.description: The Yaki Onigiri are compacted and golden rice triangles on the plate to form a dry crust. Soy sauce, mirin and butter are added during the finish for a salty and glossy glaze. The soy sauce is brushed on both sides during the grilling, while the butter smells like the crust of the onigiri.
recipe_000101.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Yuru Camp△, Log Horizon. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Use freshly cooked rice but warm enough to be handled; moisten and slightly salt your hands.
stepTexts.step_2: Divide the rice into four portions and form compact triangles, pressing as much as necessary because they do not break during the grilling.
stepTexts.step_3: Mix soy sauce and mirin in a bowl and prepare a kitchen brush.
stepTexts.step_4: Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan and brown the oniri over medium heat for about 3 minutes per side, without moving them until a crust is formed.
stepTexts.step_5: Brush one side with the mixture of soy, turn and leave caramel for about 1 minute; repeat on the other side.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the remaining butter and turn the onigiri into the pan to distribute the scent without burning the sauce.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with toasted sesame and hot servants, with dry crust and still soft center.

recipe_000102.title: Dashimaki Tamago — rolled Japanese omelet with dashi
recipe_000102.description: The Dashi Maki Tamago is a Japanese omelet rolled in thin layers with dashi broth, mirin and soy sauce. The subsequent egg additions are made to the roll and wrapped on the roll, then the omelet is molded and cut into slices. The roll is formed with several successive layers of egg in the same pan, then is molded and sliced with care.
recipe_000102.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Midnight Diner. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: In a bowl, gently beat the eggs with the dashi, mirin, soy sauce and salt, without whipping in air.
stepTexts.step_2: Filter the mixture with a strainer to make it perfectly homogeneous.
stepTexts.step_3: Grease a rectangular frying pan (makiyakinabe) with absorbent paper soaked in oil over medium-low heat.
stepTexts.step_4: Add a thin layer of egg, have it retract slightly and roll towards you.
stepTexts.step_5: Place the roll on the bottom, grease the pan again and add another layer by pouring the egg under the roll.
stepTexts.step_6: Repeat the operation 4-5 times until the roll becomes high and stratified.
stepTexts.step_7: Shape with a bamboo mat, cut into thick slices and serve with grated daikon and soy sauce.

recipe_000103.title: Layered Matcha Parfait
recipe_000103.description: The Matcha Parfait layers matcha ice cream, sweet red-bean paste (anko), cubes of matcha jelly and other toppings in a tall glass. Prepare and chill the jelly and shiratama in advance; assemble the layers and add the finishing garnishes just before serving. Matcha jelly and shiratama should be prepared in advance; ice cream and waffle arrive just before serving.
recipe_000103.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by K-On!, Gintama. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

corn_flakes_o_fiocchi_di_cereali_croccan.name: Corn flakes or crispy cereal flakes

cialde_o_bastoncini_pocky_al_matcha_per_.name: waffles or pocky sticks to the matcha to garnish

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare and cool in advance matcha and shiratama gelatin; mount the soft cream and keep the ice cream in the freezer until the last one.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the gelatin into regular cubes and divide l'anko into two portions, so the layers will be balanced in the two glasses.
stepTexts.step_3: Put a thin layer of corn flakes on the bottom of the glasses, avoiding crushing them.
stepTexts.step_4: Add gelatin to the matcha, anko and a first spoonful of whipped cream, leaving the layers visible.
stepTexts.step_5: Repeat the layers if the height of the glass allows, without filling it completely.
stepTexts.step_6: Add an ice cream ball to the matcha only at the time of service.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with shiratama, waffle or Pocky and a small tuft of cream; serve immediately so that the crispy part does not lose consistency.

recipe_000104.title: Kabocha Korokke — Japanese pumpkin croquettes
recipe_000104.description: The Kabocha Korokke are Japanese pumpkin nuggets steamed and crushed, enriched with minced meat and onion. After forming and breading they are fried until gilding and served with tonkatsu sauce. The pumpkin is molded in croquettes, flour, egg and panko, then fried until you get a golden crust.
recipe_000104.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Kiki - Consegne a domicilio, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the pumpkin into pieces and let it steam for 15 minutes until it becomes tender.
stepTexts.step_2: Then crush it with a potato crusher holding the skin and eliminating excess moisture.
stepTexts.step_3: Burn onion and minced meat in butter until well cooked and season with salt and pepper.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the meat to the pumpkin puree, mix well and let cool the dough.
stepTexts.step_5: Shape 6 oval and crushed croquettes.
stepTexts.step_6: Pass each croquette into the flour, then into the beaten egg and finally into the panko pressing well.
stepTexts.step_7: Fry in abundant hot oil at 170°C until full crispy gilding (about 3 minutes per side).
stepTexts.step_8: Serve hot with tonkatsu sauce.

recipe_000105.title: Nerikiri — traditional Japanese wagashi sweets
recipe_000105.description: The Nerikiri is a small sweet molded with shiroan white bean paste and a base of glutinous rice flour. Each portion is spread out, filled with anko and handmade in decorative forms, to be served with tea. The blackikiri is hand-molded around the anko, with small wagashi tools that draw petals and details on the surface.
recipe_000105.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Kimi ni Todoke. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

anko.name: Anko (red bean paste) for central filling

stepTexts.step_1: Melt the shiratamako in the water until the lumps are removed, then incorporate it with the shiroan in a non-stick pan.
stepTexts.step_2: Cook over very low heat stirring and crushing the mixture until it loses moisture, becomes elastic and comes off the pan.
stepTexts.step_3: Transfer the dough onto a tray and work it several times as it cools to obtain a smooth and uniform mass.
stepTexts.step_4: Divide it into the necessary portions and color small parts with minimal amounts of dye, kneading until the dye is homogeneous.
stepTexts.step_5: Form four balls of anko from about 15 g each and keep them covered so that they do not dry out.
stepTexts.step_6: Flatten a portion of nerikiri, place the anko filling in the centre and seal the seam firmly underneath.
stepTexts.step_7: Model the surface with toothpick or wagashi tools to create petals and details, working with barely wet hands.
stepTexts.step_8: Keep covered and serve at room temperature with tea, preferably on the same day.

recipe_000106.title: Yaki-Imo — Japanese roasted sweet potatoes
recipe_000106.description: The Yaki-Imo is obtained by slowly cooking the Japanese sweet potatoes with the peel. The prolonged cooking concentrates the sweetness and leaves the flesh soft, to be consumed hot without filling. The paper preserves the steam during rest, completing the softness of the sweet potato before opening and dividing it.
recipe_000106.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by My Neighbor Totoro, Yuru Camp△. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

patata_dolci_giapponesi_a_pasta_viola_gi.name: Japanese sweet potatoes with purple/yellow paste (Satsumaimo)

stepTexts.step_1: Choose similar sizes, wash them carefully without peeling them and dry them well.
stepTexts.step_2: Bucherella the skin in some places with a toothpick to facilitate a uniform cooking.
stepTexts.step_3: For a creamier pulp, wrap each potato in freshly moist kitchen paper and then in aluminium; for a dry skin, use only aluminium.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook in a static oven at 180-190°C for about 60-75 minutes, turning the paperwork in half cooking.
stepTexts.step_5: Check by sticking a toothpick into the thickest point: it must enter without resistance and the pulp must be soft to the center.
stepTexts.step_6: Leave to stand closed in the paper for 5-10 minutes, so the steam completes the cooking.
stepTexts.step_7: Open, divide in half and serve hot; the salt is optional and should only be added to the service.

recipe_000107.title: Ogura Toast — thick toast with sweet red bean paste
recipe_000107.description: The Ogura Toast is a thick slice of toasted shokupan, coated with butter and covered with sweet ogura-an red bean paste. It is served immediately after the cut, when the bread is still warm and contrasts with the filling. The toast remains crispy under the ogura an; any cream should be added cold only when the toast is warmed.
recipe_000107.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Dagashi Kashi. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

spesse_di_pane_per_toast_giapponese_shok.name: thick bread for Japanese toast Shokupan

burro_di_ottima_qualita_a_temperatura_am.name: excellent quality butter at room temperature

confettura_di_fagioli_rossi_ogura_an.name: Ogura An red bean jam (anko with whole beans)

stepTexts.step_1: Cut two slices of shokupan thick about 2"3 cm and bring l"ogura an to room temperature or just heat it, without letting it dry.
stepTexts.step_2: If the anko is very compact, soften it with a teaspoon of hot water and stir until it is creamy but not liquid.
stepTexts.step_3: Toast the bread on both sides until the surface is well golden and crispy while the center remains soft.
stepTexts.step_4: Sprinkle the butter on the still hot bread immediately, insisting also on the edges so that it is absorbed by the crumb.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute l'ogura an in a generous and uniform layer, without crushing the bread.
stepTexts.step_6: If you use whipped cream, add it cold only after letting the toast cool for a minute, so it doesn't melt.
stepTexts.step_7: Diagonally cut and serve immediately, keeping the contrast between crispy crust, soft bread, butter and anko.

recipe_000108.title: Tonkotsu Ramen — rich pork-bone broth ramen
recipe_000108.description: The Tonkotsu Ramen requires a broth of cooked pork bones for a long time until it becomes dense and milky. The noodles boil separately and are completed with chashu, ajitama and seals; the long extraction of the broth precedes the final assembly. The altar is distributed in the bowls before the very hot broth, then come noodles, chashu, ajitama and a few drops of mayu.
recipe_000108.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! (Shokugeki no Soma), Ramen Daisuki Koizumi-san. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

brodo_ossa_di_maiale_miste_collo_femore_.name: mixed pig bones (neck, femur or knuckle)

brodo_acqua_fredda_piu_acqua_bollente_pe.name: cold water, plus boiling water for rackets

stepTexts.step_1: Rinse the pig bones and leave them in cold water for 15-30 minutes, changing the water several times to remove blood and impurities.
stepTexts.step_2: Boil the bones 10 minutes, drain and rinse thoroughly; also clean the pot before starting the actual broth.
stepTexts.step_3: Cover the bones with fresh water, add garlic and ginger and bring to a vigorous boiling; foam the dark clots in the early stages.
stepTexts.step_4: Keep a firm boil for at least 5-6 hours, bubbling with boiling water when needed: fat and collagen must emulsify until the broth is opaque and full-bodied.
stepTexts.step_5: Filter the broth, put it back on the fire and adjust the concentration; prepare to partear, chashu, eggs, sprouts, onion, nori and mayu oil.
stepTexts.step_6: Bring to a boil a separate pot of water and cook the fresh noodles for the indicated time, usually 1-2 minutes; drain them very well.
stepTexts.step_7: Place the torre on the bottom of the preheated bowls, pour the boiling tonkotsu broth and mix.
stepTexts.step_8: Add the noodles and complete immediately with chashu, half ajitama, buds, onion, nori and a few drops of mayu.

recipe_000109.title: Kurogoma Ice Cream — black sesame ice cream
recipe_000109.description: The Kurogoma Ice Cream is a black sesame ice cream obtained by incorporating toasted sesame paste with a base of milk, cream and sugar. The mixture is cooled and maintained; without ice cream maker it requires mixing during freezing to limit ice crystals. The black sesame base is lightened by incorporating cream; without ice cream maker it mixes during freezing to limit its crystals.
recipe_000109.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Gintama. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Mix milk, sugar and salt in a saucepan and heat them over medium heat until the sugar is completely dissolved, without boiling.
stepTexts.step_2: Embed the black sesame paste with a whisk until a uniform base is obtained without lumps.
stepTexts.step_3: It cools the mixture quickly, first at room temperature and then in the refrigerator until it is cold.
stepTexts.step_4: Mount the cream up to a soft consistency, not excessively firm.
stepTexts.step_5: It incorporates the cream at the base of sesame in two or three times with delicate movements, maintaining the airy compound.
stepTexts.step_6: With ice cream maker, keep until the consistency expected by the manufacturer and transfer to freezer to stabilize.
stepTexts.step_7: Without ice cream maker, freeze in a low container and mix vigorously every 30 minutes for about 2 hours, then let completely firm before serving.

recipe_000110.title: Motsunabe — Fukuoka-style offal and leek hotpot
recipe_000110.description: The Motsunabe cooks tripe or other clean offals together with cabbage, Chinese leeks and aromas in a tasty broth. The preparation of the offal requires special attention before cooking; the vegetables are added in time to remain recognizable. The nira is added in the last minutes of cooking the offal, which require careful cleaning before entering the broth.
recipe_000110.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Golden Kamuy. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

trippa_o_frattaglie_di_manzo_maiale_puli.name: Trippe or offal of clean beef/pig

stepTexts.step_1: Clean the offal thoroughly; rub them with salt and little flour, rinse them several times and cut them into regular bites. Use only tripe/offal sold already cleaned and precooked, following the producer's directions. The 10–15 minutes are for final heating, NOT sufficient to cook raw offal safely; raw offal requires its own complete cooking beforehand.
stepTexts.step_2: Boil it for about 1 minute, drain and rinse: this phase eliminates impurities and part of the smell without melting the fat too much.
stepTexts.step_3: Prepare the broth with dashi, garlic, chilli and miso or soy sauce. Season it well, as the cabbage and tofu will dilute the flavour.
stepTexts.step_4: Place the cabbage on the bottom of the nabe, add tofu and offal and pour the broth until you partially cover the ingredients.
stepTexts.step_5: Bring to the boil and cook the offal for about 10-15 minutes, until they become swollen and tender.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the nira cut into sticks in the last few minutes, without mixing too much.
stepTexts.step_7: Taste the broth, adjust the miso or soy and serve the boiling nabe directly from the pot.

recipe_000111.title: Saba no Misoni — mackerel braised with miso and ginger
recipe_000111.description: The Saba no Misoni is mackerel stewed in a sauce of miso, mirin and ginger. The fish is burned and then cooked gently in the bottom, which shrinks without breaking the fillets; it is completed with fresh ginger. The miso is dissolved in part of the bottom before returning to the mackerel; the sauce thickens without aggressive boiling.
recipe_000111.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Cooking Papa. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Slightly insert the skin of the mackerel fillets and pour boiling water over it for a few seconds; drain and dry them to mitigate the most intense smell.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the ginger into thin slices and prepare in a large pan water or dashi, sake, mirin and sugar.
stepTexts.step_3: Bring the liquid to a boil and add half the ginger.
stepTexts.step_4: Place the mackerel with the skin facing upwards, cover with an otoshibuta or perforated baking paper and cook over medium to low heat for about 8-10 minutes.
stepTexts.step_5: Take a ladle from the bottom, melt the miso and put it back in the pan without boiling it violently.
stepTexts.step_6: Continue napping the fillets with the bottom for 3-5 minutes, until the sauce becomes shiny and slightly dense.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with the ginger left and serve immediately, with the skin intact and the meat still juicy.

recipe_000112.title: Chashu Don — braised pork and egg rice bowl
recipe_000112.description: The Chashu Don puts on Japanese rice hot slices of braised and heated chashu pork in its bottom. Part of the cooking sauce is poured on the meat; egg and seals complete the dish to be served immediately. The chashu is served on the still hot rice with ajitama and onion, avoiding that the braised fat cools.
recipe_000112.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Naruto, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

ciotola_riso_giapponese_cotto_e_ben_cald.name: Japanese rice cooked and well warm

stepTexts.step_1: Heat the chashu in a frying pan with a tablespoon of its soup sauce until the fat returns soft and the edges begin to caramelize.
stepTexts.step_2: If you use slices instead of cubes, doral quickly on both sides or pass them with the cinnamon to obtain a more aromatic surface.
stepTexts.step_3: Distribute the very hot rice into the bowls and season with some of the lard sauce.
stepTexts.step_4: Place the chashu over the rice without crowding it, so that every bite receives meat and sauce.
stepTexts.step_5: Cut the jitama in half and add it to the bowl.
stepTexts.step_6: Complete with sliced onion and, if expected, a small amount of mayonnaise Kewpie.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve immediately before the chashu's fat cools and repents.

recipe_000113.title: Ebi Mayo — crispy shrimp in sweet-and-tangy mayo sauce
recipe_000113.description: The Ebi Mayo are shrimps with a thin crust of starch and white, fried and then covered with a creamy mayonnaise sauce with a sweet and sour taste. The sauce is added at the end, so the shrimps remain warm and slightly crispy. The mayo ebi sauce covers the shrimps still warm immediately after frying, without letting them rest until softening the crust.
recipe_000113.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Isekai Izakaya Nobu. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Dry the shrimp well and practice a small cut on the back if necessary to remove the intestinal thread.
stepTexts.step_2: Mix Kewpie mayonnaise, condensed milk or honey and lemon juice until you get a smooth sauce; keep it aside at cool temperature.
stepTexts.step_3: It passes the shrimps into the album and then into the cornstarch, eliminating the excess to obtain a thin coating.
stepTexts.step_4: Bring the oil to about 170°C and fry a few shrimps at a time for 2-3 minutes, until they are just golden and cooked in the center.
stepTexts.step_5: Drain onto grid or absorbent paper and let them rest only a few seconds.
stepTexts.step_6: Condiscile still warm with the sauce Ebi Mayo, stirring gently to cover them without softening the crust too much.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve immediately, with lemon peel or onion as a finish.

recipe_000114.title: Nagashi Somen — chilled summer somen noodles
recipe_000114.description: The Nagashi Somen are very thin noodles boiled and cooled quickly, served with coldmentsuyu sauce and aromas such as ginger and onion. Typical service in running water can be simulated, while the dressing is offered separately to dip the pasta. The somen are quickly cooled and served in small portions, accompanied by cold mentsuyu and fresh aromas.
recipe_000114.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Non Non Biyori, Karakkai Jozu no Takagi-san. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the mentsuyu in advance and cool it well in the refrigerator; grate the ginger and slice the onion just before the service.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring to a boil abundant unsalted water and immerse the somen, separating them immediately with the chopsticks.
stepTexts.step_3: Cook them for about 90 seconds or according to the package: they must remain elastic and not disassemble.
stepTexts.step_4: Drains and washes under very cold running water, gently rubbing them with your hands to remove surface starch.
stepTexts.step_5: Transfer them to water and ice just to keep them cool, without leaving them immersed too long.
stepTexts.step_6: Serve small portions at a time and dip them in the cold mentsuyu with ginger, onion and sesame.
stepTexts.step_7: If you want to simulate the nagashi service, scroll the somen in very cold clean water and collect them immediately with chopsticks.

recipe_000115.title: Classic Anmitsu — kanten jelly, fruit, anko and kuromitsu
recipe_000115.description: The Anmitsu combines kanten jelly cubes, fruit and red bean paste in a cup. The kanten must be boiled, solidified and cut in advance; the kuromitsu syrup is poured only at the service. Kanten cubes remain visible next to fruit and shiratama, while kuromitsu is poured only at the time of eating.
recipe_000115.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Gintama, Demon Slayer. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

acqua_per_kanten.name: water
acqua_per_kanten.note: To dissolve and activate the kanten.

stepTexts.step_1: Melt the kanten in cold water, bring to a boil and cook for about 2 minutes stirring until it is completely dispersed.
stepTexts.step_2: Pour the liquid into a low container, let cool and transfer to the refrigerator until complete gelling.
stepTexts.step_3: Cut the kanten gelatin into regular cubes and prepare the fruit by dripping it well.
stepTexts.step_4: If you use shiratama, cook until it floats, continue for 1-2 minutes and cool them in cold water.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute kanten cubes into cups and add fruit and shiratama while keeping the different elements visible.
stepTexts.step_6: Add a portion of anko to the center.
stepTexts.step_7: Pour the kuromitsu only at the time of service, so jelly and fruit do not remain immersed too long.

recipe_000116.title: Kinpira Gobo — sautéed burdock root and carrots
recipe_000116.description: In the Kimpira Gobo thin sticks of bardana and carrot are quickly salted and flavored with soy sauce, mirin and sesame. The consistency remains slightly crisp; shichimi and toasted seeds complete the vegetables. The bardana must remain slightly crisp after evaporation of the soy sauce, with sesame and shichimi added last.
recipe_000116.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Fruits Basket. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Wash and brush the bardana, cut it into a match and put it in the water immediately for about 5 minutes to limit oxidation and attenuate astringency.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the carrot into sticks of the same size and drain the beard very well.
stepTexts.step_3: Heat sesame oil in a frying pan and burdock and carrot sauce over medium to high heat for 3-4 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Add sugar and mirin and mix until the sugar is dissolved and the vegetables start to icing.
stepTexts.step_5: Pour in the soy sauce and keep jumping until the liquid has almost evaporated.
stepTexts.step_6: Taste: the bardana must be cooked but still slightly crispy.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with toasted sesame and togarashi shichimi and serve warm, warm or at room temperature.

recipe_000117.title: Tori no Karaage Namban Don — fried chicken rice bowl
recipe_000117.description: The Tori no Karaage Namban Don serves on hot rice marinated chicken bites, coated with starch and fried. The namban sauce and the final condiments add a sweet and sour note without sacrificing the crispness of the chicken. The warm karaage absorbs for a few seconds the Namban sauce, then meets the rice and the cold tartar in the same bowl.
recipe_000117.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, My Hero Academia. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

pollo_sovracosce_di_pollo_disossate_senz.name: Deboned chicken over thighs, without skin, with small mouthpieces

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the chicken thighs into regular bites and dress them with soy sauce, sake, ginger and garlic; let marinate at least 20 minutes.
stepTexts.step_2: Prepare the Namban sauce bringing to light boiling soy sauce, rice vinegar, mirin and sugar, then let it warm.
stepTexts.step_3: Prepare the tartar by mixing chopped boiled egg, onion and pickle well drained, japanese mayonnaise, little vinegar, salt and pepper; keep it in the refrigerator.
stepTexts.step_4: Drain the chicken from marinade, pass it into potato or maize starch and shake the excess.
stepTexts.step_5: Fry at 170-175°C in small lots until the bites are golden and the chicken is completely cooked; drain on grill. Check the chicken pieces with a food thermometer: the centre must reach at least 74°C (165°F). A golden crust or frying time alone does not guarantee doneness.
stepTexts.step_6: Immerse the karaage still warm in the namban sauce for a few seconds, so it absorbs the seasoning without completely losing the crispness.
stepTexts.step_7: Distribute hot rice and cabbage to julienne in the bowls, add the chicken namban and complete with the cold tartar sauce.
stepTexts.step_8: Serve immediately, keeping the contrast between hot rice, crispy chicken and fresh tartar.

recipe_000118.title: Kakuni Udon — udon noodles with tender braised pork
recipe_000118.description: The Kakuni Udon combines noodles udon in dashi broth and already braised kakuni pork, brought back to temperature in its bottom. The slices of meat are distributed on the broth with onion and little karashi mustard, to be added as desired. The braised kakuni rests on the udon covered with broth, with a spoon of its bottom and karashi served separately.
recipe_000118.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Jujutsu Kaisen, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Warm the kakuni gently in its bottom until the meat is soft and the fat is shiny again; do not boil it hard.
stepTexts.step_2: Bring the dashi to a boil and season with soy sauce and mirin, tasting before adding more salt.
stepTexts.step_3: In a separate pot cook the udon according to the package, then drain them very well.
stepTexts.step_4: Rinse the udon quickly only if required by the type used, then transfer them to the preheated bowls.
stepTexts.step_5: Pour the boiling broth on the udon and gently separate the threads with the chopsticks.
stepTexts.step_6: Add two pieces of kakuni per serving and add a spoon of the bottom of the lard to intensify the flavor.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with onion and a small amount of karashi on the edge of the bowl and serve immediately.

recipe_000119.title: Kenchinjiru — Buddhist-style vegetable, tofu and root soup
recipe_000119.description: Kenchinjiru is a vegetable soup of Japanese roots, mushrooms and crumbled tofu. The ingredients are first flavored in a saucepan and then boiled in the broth, which is completed with soy sauce and sake. The kombu dashi accompanies roots and tofu without katsuobushi, to keep vegetarian this version of the soup.
recipe_000119.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Drain the tofu and crumble it coarsely; cut daikon, carrot, gobo and shiitake into small and uniform pieces.
stepTexts.step_2: If you use fresh gobo, briefly put it in the water after cutting and then drain it well.
stepTexts.step_3: Heat sesame oil in casserole and brown before the roots and mushrooms for 3-4 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the tofu and mix gently to cover it with oil without reducing it to cream.
stepTexts.step_5: Pour the kombu dashi, bring to light boil and remove the foam that emerges.
stepTexts.step_6: Bake over low heat for about 15 minutes, until the roots are tender but not undone.
stepTexts.step_7: Season with sake and soy sauce, taste and serve hot; avoid katsuobushi if you want to keep the preparation strictly vegetarian.

recipe_000120.title: Omusoba — yakisoba wrapped in an omelet
recipe_000120.description: The Omusoba contains a portion of yakisoba with vegetables and meat under a thin omelette. The noodles are first skipped with their sauce; the omelet is cooked separately and settles on the pasta just before serving. The omelet wraps a portion of yakisoba and is turned with the closure underneath, before receiving sauces and honors.
recipe_000120.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Ranma ½. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Slice cabbage and carrot, cut the pig into bites and separate the yakisoba noodles with your hands.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat a large frying pan, brown the pork and add the carrot, cabbage and any sprouts. Stir-fry until the vegetables begin to soften.
stepTexts.step_3: Add the noodles and a few tablespoons of water, cover for 1-2 minutes and then separate them completely.
stepTexts.step_4: Season with yakisoba sauce and skip until the bottom is dry and the noodles are well coated; put aside the heat.
stepTexts.step_5: Beat the eggs with milk and a pinch of salt, then cook in a clean frying pan a thin omelette still soft in the middle.
stepTexts.step_6: Place a portion of yakisoba in the center of the omelet, fold the edges and reverse on the plate with the closing down.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with yakisoba sauce, Kewpie mayonnaise and aonori; add shoga or katsuobushi goods if expected.
stepTexts.step_8: Serve immediately before the omelet dries.

recipe_000121.title: Japanese Soufflé Cheesecake — cotton-soft cheesecake
recipe_000121.description: The Japanese Cheesecake Soufflé combines spreadable cheese, egg yolks and egg whites mounted to obtain a high and light cake. Bain-bath cooking and gradual cooling in the oven help to preserve the soft structure. The bain-marie cooking keeps the center soft, while the gradual cooling in the open oven precedes the cutting.
recipe_000121.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, K-On!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

uovo.name: egg (separate egg yolks and egg yolks)

stepTexts.step_1: Dress the mold and prepare a larger baking tray for the water bath; preheat the oven to 150-160°C.
stepTexts.step_2: Melt in a bainmaria cheese spreadable, butter and milk until the mixture is smooth, then let cool.
stepTexts.step_3: Embed the egg yolks one at a time and add sifted flour and starch, stirring only until the lumps are removed.
stepTexts.step_4: Mount the egg whites and add sugar in several shots until you get a shiny meringue with soft-medium peaks, not excessively rigid.
stepTexts.step_5: Embed a third of the meringue at the base to lighten it, then join the rest with movements from bottom to top.
stepTexts.step_6: Pour into the mold, remove the larger bubbles with small blows and place the mold in the hot water bath.
stepTexts.step_7: Cook for about 60 minutes, adjusting the heat if the surface darkens too much; the center must be cooked but still elastic.
stepTexts.step_8: Turn off the oven and let the cake stand with the open door open for 10-15 minutes, then deform and cool it completely before cutting.

recipe_000122.title: Suika Shiratama — watermelon with rice dumplings and lemon syrup
recipe_000122.description: The Suika Shiratama is a summer dessert of cold watermelon, rice mochi balls and lemon soda. The shiratamas are boiled and cooled first, then joined to the fruit at the time of service to maintain freshness and consistency. Shiratama and watermelon are distributed in cold glasses, adding the sparkling drink only when serving them.
recipe_000122.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Grand Blue, Free!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

sciroppo_di_seltz_o_sprite.name: Seltz or lemon soda
sciroppo_di_seltz_o_sprite.note: Use a cold drink; the lemon soda makes the dessert sweeter.

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the shiratamas by mixing glutinous rice flour and water little at a time until you get a soft and modelable dough.
stepTexts.step_2: It forms small balls, cook them in boiling water until they come up to the surface and continue for 1-2 minutes; immediately cool them in water and ice.
stepTexts.step_3: Cut the watermelon into cubes or small balls, remove the seeds and cool it in the refrigerator.
stepTexts.step_4: Drain the shiratamas and dry them slightly so that the drink is not diluted.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute watermelon and shiratama in very cold glasses.
stepTexts.step_6: Add cold seltz or a transparent lemon drink only at the time of service.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve immediately with a teaspoon or wide straw; keep the dessert cold but do not leave the shiratama immersed for hours.

recipe_000123.title: Tori Zosui — chicken, rice and egg soup in dashi broth
recipe_000123.description: The Tori Zosui is a delicate soup of rice already cooked, chicken and egg in dashi broth. The rice is eventually rinsed to check the starch, while chicken and egg cook in the liquid before adding fresh onion. The egg is flushed over the rice and ends cooking with the heat of the covered soup.
recipe_000123.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Barakamon, Gintama. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

brodo_dashi_insaporito_con_soia_e_mirin_.name: flavored dashi broth with soy sauce

stepTexts.step_1: If cooked rice is very starchy, rinse it quickly under cold water and drain it; this keeps the zosui lighter.
stepTexts.step_2: Cut the chicken into thin strips and bring the dashi to light boil with soy sauce and mirin.
stepTexts.step_3: Add the chicken and cook for about 4-5 minutes, removing any foam.
stepTexts.step_4: Combine the rice and simmer another 4-5 minutes, stirring just enough to not break the beans.
stepTexts.step_5: Beat the egg without making it completely homogeneous and flush it over the surface.
stepTexts.step_6: Turn off the heat, cover for about 1 minute and let the egg finish cooking with the residual heat.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with onion and serve immediately, when the rice is soft but not yet fucked.

recipe_000124.title: Uni Don — fresh sea urchin over rice
recipe_000124.description: Uni Don presents sea urchin roe over gently cooled Japanese sushi rice. Use only uni expressly suitable for raw consumption and keep it refrigerated until assembly; do not rely on tasting or smell to establish safety. Divide the warm—not hot—rice between bowls with strips of nori, arrange the uni delicately in a single layer, and serve with wasabi and soy sauce on the side.
recipe_000124.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Golden Kamuy. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Use very fresh and keep it refrigerated until assembly; gently remove any excess liquid without crushing the gonads.
stepTexts.step_2: Prepare the Japanese rice, season it as indicated if you use sushi rice and let it warm up covered: it must be warm, not boiling.
stepTexts.step_3: Check that the uni is expressly suitable for raw consumption and has been stored according to the supplier's instructions. Do not taste it to assess safety: neither smell nor flavour is sufficient evidence.
stepTexts.step_4: Distribute rice into bowls without compressing it and add thin strips of nori.
stepTexts.step_5: Arrange the languages of one in one layer, handling them as little as possible to keep them intact.
stepTexts.step_6: Add a small amount of wasabi to the side, not directly on the whole hedgehog.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve the soy sauce separately or pour very little by thread only at the time of eating, so the delicate flavor of the uni remains the protagonist.

recipe_000125.title: Choco Cornet — soft bread cones filled with chocolate
recipe_000125.description: Choco Cornet is a sweet brioche sandwich wrapped on cone moulds and cooked until golden. Only after cooling the wrap is filled with thick chocolate cream, preventing the filling from melting. Pasta cones must cool completely before receiving the chocolate cream, which would otherwise lose consistency.
recipe_000125.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Lucky Star, Sound! Euphonium. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the brioche dough with flour, milk, yeast, sugar, egg, salt and butter; mix until it becomes smooth and elastic.
stepTexts.step_2: Cover and let rise until doubling, usually 60-90 minutes depending on the temperature.
stepTexts.step_3: Meanwhile, prepare a thick chocolate cream, cool it completely and transfer it to a sac à poche.
stepTexts.step_4: Gently deflate the dough, divide it into portions and form long and regular cords.
stepTexts.step_5: Slightly grease the cone molds and wrap each spiral cord, just overlapping the spins without leaving cracks.
stepTexts.step_6: Leave the shaped croissants to stand for 20-30 minutes, then brush them with beaten egg.
stepTexts.step_7: Bake at 180°C for about 12-15 minutes, until they are uniformly golden; cool a few minutes and remove the moulds.
stepTexts.step_8: Let cool completely before filling with chocolate cream, so the filling does not melt.

recipe_000126.title: Kushikatsu — Osaka-style crispy fried skewers
recipe_000126.description: The Kushikatsu are meat skewers, shrimps and fried and breaded vegetables until you get a uniform crust. The pieces are cut in similar sizes and infiltrated before the breading; the sauce is used separately. The skewers are fried a few at a time and drained on the grill; meat and shrimp require a verification of the cooking in the center.
recipe_000126.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Isekai Izakaya Nobu. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Cut pork, shrimp, onion and lotus root into similar pieces, small enough to cook at the same time, and put them separately on skewers.
stepTexts.step_2: Dry all the ingredients and flour slightly to favor the adhesion of the batter.
stepTexts.step_3: Prepare a fluid batter with flour, egg and cold water, without working too hard.
stepTexts.step_4: Pass every skewer into the batter and then into the panko, pressing just to create a uniform layer.
stepTexts.step_5: Bring the oil to 170-175°C and fry a few skewers at a time, adjusting the times according to the ingredient.
stepTexts.step_6: Drain on the grill and let stand for one minute; check that meat and shrimp are cooked in the middle.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve hot with kushikatsu sauce or tonkatsu separately, avoiding to leave the skewers immersed in the sauce.

recipe_000127.title: Mizumochi / Raindrop Cake — clear water jelly
recipe_000127.description: The Mizumochi, or Raindrop Cake, is a very delicate water gelatin thickened with agar-agar and molded in transparent forms. After the firming it is immediately used with kinako and kuromitsu added to the side in order not to hide its appearance. The transparent gelatin must be completely firmed in the refrigerator before being disformed, with kinako and kuromitsu served to the side.
recipe_000127.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Demon Slayer. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

mochi_d_acqua_agar_agar_in_polvere_2.name: agar-agar powder
mochi_d_acqua_agar_agar_in_polvere_2.note: The gelling force varies between brands: if the product indicates a different minimum dosage, follow the manufacturer's report while maintaining a very soft geling.

stepTexts.step_1: Mix water, agar/kanten and any small amount of sugar in a saucepan before turning on the fire.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat by stirring until boiling and keep a slight boiling for as long as it takes to completely melt l'agar, usually a few minutes.
stepTexts.step_3: Turn off and briefly let the liquid rest to raise the bubbles, eliminating them with a spoon if necessary.
stepTexts.step_4: Pour into spherical molds or small cups without incorporating air.
stepTexts.step_5: Let cool and transfer to the refrigerator for at least 2-4 hours until the gelatin is fully stabilized.
stepTexts.step_6: Shape with great delicacy directly on the serving plate.
stepTexts.step_7: Add kinako and kuromitsu to the side only at the last moment and serve cold.

recipe_000128.title: Apple and Cocoa Japanese Curry Stew
recipe_000128.description: This Japanese curry slowly cooks meat, onion and grated apple in a sauce enriched with little bitter cocoa. The sweetness of the apple balances the spicy notes of the roux, and the dish is served with steamed white rice. The roux melts over heat off, while cocoa and apple contribute to the sauce that then simmers slowly next to the rice.
recipe_000128.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars! (Shokugeki no Soma), Persona 5. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

cacao_amaro_in_polvere.name: Bitter cocoa powder (or 2 squares of dark chocolate 70%)

noce_di_roux_per_curry_giapponese.name: roux nut for Japanese curry (or curry powder + flour)

riso_bianco_cotto_al_vapore.name: steamed white rice (to serve)
riso_bianco_cotto_al_vapore.note: about 160 g of cooked rice per serving

stepTexts.step_1: In a large pot, brown the onions with a little oil until they become well golden and caramelized.
stepTexts.step_2: Combine the meat with cubes and brown it on all sides.
stepTexts.step_3: Insert the carrots and potatoes.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the meat broth and the grated apple.
stepTexts.step_5: Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes.
stepTexts.step_6: Turn off the heat, join the roux for curry and amalgam until complete dissolution.
stepTexts.step_7: Combine the bitter cocoa powder (or dark chocolate), mix well and cook over very slow heat for another 5 minutes until you get a thick, shiny and aromatic sauce.
stepTexts.step_8: Bring to the hot table accompanied by white steamed rice.

recipe_000129.title: Niku Soba — hot soba noodles with pork and leeks
recipe_000129.description: Niku Soba is a buckwheat noodles soup with thin slices of pork and toasted leeks. The hot broth is prepared separately and poured on the soba cotta, along with the cooked meat and aromas. The soba is boiled separately and transferred into the very hot broth with pork and grilled leek, finished with shichimi.
recipe_000129.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

pancia_o_lonza_di_maiale_affettata_sotti.name: very thin sliced pork belly or pork loin

shichimi_togarashi.name: Shichimi Togarashi (spice seven flavors, to garnish)

stepTexts.step_1: In a non-stick pan without added fats, grill the leek spools until they are golden and toast them slightly on the surface, keep aside.
stepTexts.step_2: Put in a saucepan, boil the Dashi broth with soy sauce, mirin and sugar.
stepTexts.step_3: Combine the pork slices and let them cook for 3-4 minutes until they are tender.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook soba in plenty of boiling water for the time indicated on the package (about 3-4 minutes), drain and rinse briefly.
stepTexts.step_5: Divide the soba into two large bowls.
stepTexts.step_6: Add over the boiling broth with the pork slices and garnish with the grilled leek and a sprinkle of Shichimi Togarashi.

recipe_000130.title: Ebi Tempura Udon — udon soup with shrimp tempura
recipe_000130.description: The Ebi Tempura Udon combines noodles udon in freshly fried dashi broth and shrimps in tempura. The cold batter must remain light and the frying is completed shortly before the service, so the crust remains crunchy on the soup. The tempura of shrimps settles on the udon only at the end, preserving the crunchy crust away from the broth until serving.
recipe_000130.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Mob Psycho 100. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

gamberone_freschi.name: Fresh prawns (clean and peeled, keeping tail)

farina_per_tempura.name: tempura flour (or Italian 00 flour + iced water)

stepTexts.step_1: Clean the shrimp leaving the tail, remove the intestinal thread and practice small cuts on the belly to keep them straight in frying.
stepTexts.step_2: Prepare the broth by bringing dashi, light soy sauce and mirin to light sob; keep it warm without reducing it too much.
stepTexts.step_3: Mix tempura flour and ice water quickly, leaving a few small lumps and keeping the batter cold.
stepTexts.step_4: Take the oil to about 170°C, pass the shrimps into the batter and fry them a few at a time for about 2 minutes, until they are light and crispy.
stepTexts.step_5: Drain the tempura on the grid without covering it.
stepTexts.step_6: Cook the udon in separate water, drain well and distribute them in the bowls.
stepTexts.step_7: Pour the boiling broth on the udon and add onion.
stepTexts.step_8: It adapts the shrimps in tempura only at the time of serving, so the crust remains crunchy longer.

recipe_000131.title: Hiyashi Tanuki Udon — chilled udon with crunchy tenkasu
recipe_000131.description: The Hiyashi Tanuki Udon are thick noodles served cold with meatsuyu sauce, cucumber and crunchy tenkasu. Udons are cooled and drained well; seasoning and crunchies are added only at the time of eating. The tenkasu is added just before the cold mentsuyu, so it remains crispy next to the udons and vegetables.
recipe_000131.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by March Comes in Like a Lion, Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

uovo_sodo_o_uovo_cotto_a_bassa_temperatu.name: boiled egg or boiled egg at low temperature (Onsen Tamago)

salsa_mentsuyu_concentrata.name: Mentsuyu concentrated sauce (colded in the fridge)

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the mentsuyu and let it cool completely in the refrigerator; cucumber slice, onion and nori and keep the tenkasu dry until serving.
stepTexts.step_2: Cook the udon in plenty of boiling water as long as they are elastic but still consistent.
stepTexts.step_3: Drain and cool immediately under very cold running water, then pass them in water and ice to stop completely cooking.
stepTexts.step_4: Drain the udon with care and shake them well: the residual water would dilute the mentsuyu.
stepTexts.step_5: Distribute them in the bowls and add cucumber, egg, onion and nori.
stepTexts.step_6: Add tenkasu only at the last moment, so it remains crispy.
stepTexts.step_7: Pour the cold mentsuyu immediately before serving and mix at the table.

recipe_000132.title: Katsu Curry Sando — breaded cutlet sandwich with curry sauce
recipe_000132.description: The Katsu Curry Sando combines soft shokupan bread with a crunchy tonkatsu and thick curry sauce. The sandwich is hot-assembled with well-drained filling and cut before moisture softens the breading. A short pressure compacts the sandwich without crushing the tonkatsu, which must keep the crispy bread between the slices of bread.
recipe_000132.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Chainsaw Man, Spy x Family. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

salsa_curry_denso.name: thick curry sauce (or Tonkatsu sauce mixed with little curry)

stepTexts.step_1: Keep ready the freshly fried or well heated tonkatsu cutlets, still crispy, and prepare the finely sliced cabbage.
stepTexts.step_2: Spread a thin veil of butter on the inside of the shokupan slices to create a barrier against moisture.
stepTexts.step_3: Season the cutlet with a thick curry sauce, avoiding excessive soaking of the breading.
stepTexts.step_4: Distribute the cabbage on the first slice of bread and place over the hot tonkatsu.
stepTexts.step_5: Close the sandwich, wrap it slightly with baking paper and press with a moderate weight for about 2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_6: Cut the crusts if you want a more traditional shape and cut the sandwich with a very sharp knife.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve immediately, when the bread is soft and the tonkatsu still preserves crunchiness.

recipe_000133.title: Tori Chashu Ramen — ramen topped with marinated chicken
recipe_000133.description: The Tori Chashu Ramen uses rolled and cooked chicken thigh in a marinade of soy sauce and aromas. The sliced chicken is placed on noodles and broth prepared separately, without confusing the cooking of the meat with the short time required by the pasta. The marinated chicken is left to cool and sliced before mounting with hot broth, noodles and marinated egg.
recipe_000133.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Ramen Daisuki Koizumi-san. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Roll the chicken thigh with the skin on the outside and tie it tightly with kitchen spaghetti.
stepTexts.step_2: Put in a saucepan, brown the roll of chicken on all sides.
stepTexts.step_3: Combine soy sauce, sake, mirin, sugar, ginger and garlic.
stepTexts.step_4: Cover and cook over low heat for 15-20 minutes by turning the chicken from time to time until the sauce thickens and glazes the meat. Before slicing the rolled chicken, verify with a food thermometer that the centre has reached at least 74°C (165°F); cook longer if necessary. Tie with kitchen twine, not edible spaghetti.
stepTexts.step_5: Let the chicken cool and slice it with gold discs.
stepTexts.step_6: Heat the chicken broth and adjust it to taste with 2 tablespoons of chicken cooking glaze.
stepTexts.step_7: Cook the noodles for ramen, drain them into the bowl, add the broth and garnish with the slices of Tori Chashu, marinated egg in half and onion.

recipe_000134.title: Shirasu Don — rice bowl with tiny whitebait and egg
recipe_000134.description: Shirasu Don combines warm Japanese rice with previously cooked shirasu (tiny whitebait fish) and a yolk from a pasteurized egg suitable for the intended use. Assemble the ingredients immediately before serving and add soy sauce sparingly. The already cooked shirasu is placed on the rice with pasteurized yolk suitable for consumption without cooking, adding soy only to the service.
recipe_000134.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by La collina dei papaveri, Midnight Diner. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

tuorlo_d_uovo_fresco.name: pasteurized egg yolk suitable for eating uncooked

stepTexts.step_1: Prepare the Japanese rice and serve it hot, then let it rest a minute in the bowl to disperse the most intense steam.
stepTexts.step_2: Drain the shirasu well and check that there is no excess liquid; if they are very salty, taste them before adding more soy sauce.
stepTexts.step_3: Prepare the garnishes before assembling: grate the ginger, finely slice the spring onion and cut the nori into strips.
stepTexts.step_4: Spread the cooked shirasu whitebait evenly over the rice without pressing them down.
stepTexts.step_5: Make a shallow well in the middle and gently add a pasteurized egg yolk suitable for eating without cooking. Do not use an unpasteurized raw yolk.
stepTexts.step_6: Add ginger, onion and nori in small separate quantities, so each bite can be adjusted as desired.
stepTexts.step_7: Pour the soy sauce flushed just before eating and partially mix the yolk with rice and shirasu, keeping different textures in the bowl.

recipe_000135.title: Agedashi Nasu — fried eggplant marinated in dashi
recipe_000135.description: The Agedashi Nasu are cut and fried eggplants, then briefly immersed in a dishi broth flavored with soy and mirin. The finish of grated daikon and fresh ginger brings freshness to the cooking bottom. Fried eggplants are seasoned in hot dash for at least ten minutes, then served with daikon and ginger.
recipe_000135.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Emiya-san Chi no Kyou no Gohan, Demon Slayer. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the eggplant in half for the long and paste the skin with shallow diagonal cuts, so that they absorb the seasoning without flaking.
stepTexts.step_2: Dry them well and bring the oil to about 170°C.
stepTexts.step_3: Fry the eggplants for 3-4 minutes, turning them once, until the pulp is soft and the skin shiny.
stepTexts.step_4: Drain on grid or absorbent paper without crushing them.
stepTexts.step_5: Bring to simmer dashi, soy sauce and mirin for 1-2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_6: Place the eggplants still warm in a container and pour over the broth, leaving them to flavor at least 10 minutes.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve warm or at room temperature with grated daikon and fresh ginger.

recipe_000136.title: Tofu Dengaku — miso-glazed tofu skewers
recipe_000136.description: The Tofu Dengaku is prepared with compact tofu well laid out, cut and stabbed, then golden before being glazed with a sweet sauce with miso. A short heat finish makes the surface shiny, to be completed with sesame. The miso glaze is applied in two steps, with a short finish under the grill to caramelize without burning the sugars.
recipe_000136.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Demon Slayer, Samurai Champloo. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Press the tofu to remove excess water, dry it and cut it into thick rectangles enough to be infiltrated without breaking.
stepTexts.step_2: Insert the skewers gently and pat the surface again.
stepTexts.step_3: Mix miso, sugar, mirin and sake in a saucepan and cook over low heat for about 2 minutes until the glaze is smooth and dense enough to stick.
stepTexts.step_4: Grill the tofu 2-3 minutes per side on a hot plate, until a slight gilding appears.
stepTexts.step_5: Brush a first time with miso sauce and let dry for about 30 seconds.
stepTexts.step_6: Add a second layer of glaze and pass under the grill for 1-2 minutes, checking continuously because the miso sugar burns easily.
stepTexts.step_7: Complete with toasted sesame and hot servi.

recipe_000137.title: Sesame and Vegetable Yakiudon
recipe_000137.description: The Yakiudon with sesame combines thick udon, cabbage and carrots blown in a pan over a lively heat. The pasta is first loosened in hot water, then quickly browned with vegetables and seasoning to maintain an elastic consistency. The sauce enters the hot edge of the wok and covers the freshly blown udon, to be served immediately with sesame and onion.
recipe_000137.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Ranma ½, My Hero Academia. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Loosen the udon noodles in boiling water for about 1 minute, drain and separate them gently without breaking them.
stepTexts.step_2: Slice cabbage, carrot and onion into thin pieces and prepare the sauces before heating the wok.
stepTexts.step_3: Heat the sesame oil over high heat and stir-fry the onion and carrot for 1–2 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Add the cabbage and continue cooking for another 2 minutes, leaving the vegetables still slightly crispy.
stepTexts.step_5: Add the udon noodles and stir-fry over high heat until thoroughly hot.
stepTexts.step_6: Pour yakisoba/tonkatsu sauce and soy sauce along the warm edge of the wok and mix quickly to cover all noodles.
stepTexts.step_7: Serve immediately with katsuobushi, sesame or onion, avoiding to leave the udon firm in the pan.

recipe_000138.title: Tonjiru — hearty pork, root vegetable and miso soup
recipe_000138.description: The Tonjiru is a hearty pork soup, daikons, carrots and other roots in broth with miso. The meat is browned and the vegetables cooked until tender, before melting the miso without unnecessarily prolonging the boiling. The miso is dissolved in a ladle of broth over a fire off, preserving the flavor of the soup with tofu and roots.
recipe_000138.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by My Hero Academia, Midnight Diner. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Cut pork belly, daikon and carrot into thin pieces and prepare the cube tofu.
stepTexts.step_2: Heat sesame oil in a saucepan and brown the pig until it changes color and releases part of the fat.
stepTexts.step_3: Add daikon and carrot and salt them for about 2 minutes to flavor them in the bottom.
stepTexts.step_4: Pour the dashi, bring to light boil and remove any foam.
stepTexts.step_5: Cover and cook over medium to low heat for about 10 minutes until the roots become tender.
stepTexts.step_6: Add the tofu and heat it for 2-3 minutes without stirring vigorously.
stepTexts.step_7: Turn off the heat, melt the miso in a ladle of broth and incorporate it to the soup without bringing it back to the boil.
stepTexts.step_8: Complete with onion and serve very hot.

recipe_000139.title: Kabocha no Nimono — simmered Japanese pumpkin
recipe_000139.description: The Kabocha no Nimono cooks pieces of japanese pumpkin with the skin in a bottom of dash, sugar and condiments. The liquid is gently reduced and the pumpkin is left to cool in the broth to absorb its flavor. The pumpkin cooks with an inner lid that keeps the liquid close to the surface; the rest favors its absorption.
recipe_000139.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Fruits Basket, Il mio vicino Totoro. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

zucca_kabocha.name: pumpkin Kabocha (or pumpkin Delica with skin)

stepTexts.step_1: Cut the pumpkin into regular touches of 3-4 cm leaving the skin (peel only slightly the edges so as not to undo it).
stepTexts.step_2: Place the pumpkin touches in one layer in a small pan with the skin pointing downwards.
stepTexts.step_3: Combine Dashi, sugar and mirin.
stepTexts.step_4: Bring to a boil, cover with an inner lid (Otoshibuta or punched oven paper) and cook for 5 minutes.
stepTexts.step_5: Add the soy sauce, cover again and cook on a sweet heat for another 8-10 minutes until the pumpkin becomes soft and the sauce is reduced.
stepTexts.step_6: Let it warm before serving so that it absorbs all flavors.

recipe_000140.title: Matcha Mille-Crêpe Cake — layered green tea crêpe cake
recipe_000140.description: The Matcha Mille Crepe Cake overlaps many thin crêpe with green tea alternating with matcha cream. After preparing and cooling the discs, the cake is layered and served cold with a dusting of matcha. The matcha crêpes are alternated with thin layers of cream and the dessert serves cold with powder tea on the surface.
recipe_000140.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by K-On!, Food Wars!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Slice flour and Matcha in a bowl.
stepTexts.step_2: Add sugar and eggs, then add warm milk and melted butter by mixing with a whisk until you get a liquid batter without lumps.
stepTexts.step_3: Rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
stepTexts.step_4: Cook about 15-20 thin crepes in a lightly buttered non-stick pan, let them cool completely.
stepTexts.step_5: Mount the cream with the icing sugar and Matcha, then incorporate it with the pastry cream.
stepTexts.step_6: Assemble the dessert by placing the first crack on a plate, spread a thin layer of cream and cover with another crack.
stepTexts.step_7: Repeat until the ingredients are exhausted.
stepTexts.step_8: Dust the surface with Matcha powder before serving cold from the refrigerator.

recipe_000141.title: Kurogoma Pudding — black sesame pudding
recipe_000141.description: Kurogoma Pudding is a soft pudding of milk, cream and black sesame paste, firmed with gelatin. The mixture is heated without boiling, filtered and left to rest in the refrigerator, then garnished with toasted sesame. The black sesame mixture is filtered before firming in the glasses, which are decorated with cream and toasted seeds.
recipe_000141.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Gintama, Saiki K.. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

stepTexts.step_1: Put the gelatin in very cold water for about 10 minutes until it is completely soft.
stepTexts.step_2: Mix milk, cream, sugar and black sesame paste in a saucepan.
stepTexts.step_3: Heat over low heat by mixing with a whisk until the mixture is uniform and the sugar is dissolved, without boiling.
stepTexts.step_4: Remove from the heat, squeeze the gelatin well and incorporate it until it is completely dissolved.
stepTexts.step_5: Filter the mixture through a fine strainer to remove any residues and obtain a smoother texture.
stepTexts.step_6: Pour in the glasses, let cool and transfer to the refrigerator for at least 3 hours.
stepTexts.step_7: Garnish with little whipped cream and toasted black sesame only at the time of service.

recipe_000142.title: Matcha Daifuku with Anko — green tea rice cakes
recipe_000142.description: The Matcha Daifuku wraps an anko ball in an elastic paste of glutinous rice flour and green tea. The dough is baked in the microwave, divided still warm and closed on the filling before being served in the day. The anko filling is wrapped in the matcha dough with the closure below, avoiding to add too much starch on the surface.
recipe_000142.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Hyouka, Fruits Basket. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

pasta_di_fagioli_rossi_anko.name: Anko red bean paste (divided into 6 balls)

stepTexts.step_1: Divide the anko into six equal balls and keep them covered; dust the work surface with corn starch or starch.
stepTexts.step_2: Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, matcha and water in a microwave bowl until dry lumps remain.
stepTexts.step_3: Cover leaving a vent and bake at 600 W for about 90 seconds.
stepTexts.step_4: Mix with a wet spatula and cook about 60 seconds, until the dough is shiny, elastic and evenly cooked.
stepTexts.step_5: Transfer immediately the hot mass to the dusted surface, cover it with other starch and let it warm enough to handle it.
stepTexts.step_6: Divide into six portions, flatten them into discs and thinn the edges slightly.
stepTexts.step_7: Put a ball of anko in the center, close the edges pinching them well and place the daifuku with the closing down.
stepTexts.step_8: Remove excess starch and serve at room temperature the same day.

recipe_000143.title: Japanese Fruit Tartlets — fresh fruit mini tarts
recipe_000143.description: The Japanese Fruit Tartlet have shell of short pastry cooked in white, filled with cold pastry cream and fresh fruit. A light gelatin shiny the surface, while the fresh storage protects the filling. Fresh fruit should be dried before decorating the cream, and neutral gelatin protects the surface without soaking the shorts.
recipe_000143.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Cardcaptor Sakura, K-On!. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

frutta_fresca_mista.name: fresh mixed fruit (frogs, kiwis, blueberries, mandarin)

stepTexts.step_1: Line the buttered tartlet moulds with shortcrust pastry, trim the edges and prick the bases with a fork.
stepTexts.step_2: Cools the shells formed for 15-20 minutes before cooking, so they keep the shape better.
stepTexts.step_3: Bake in white at 180°C for about 15-20 minutes until they are uniformly golden.
stepTexts.step_4: Shape and let cool completely on a grid.
stepTexts.step_5: Fill each cold shell with cold pastry cream, leveling it without crossing the edge.
stepTexts.step_6: Cut the fruit just before use, dry it and stock it in a compact way on the cream.
stepTexts.step_7: Brush with a veil of neutral gelatin to polish and protect the fruit.
stepTexts.step_8: Keep cool and serve in the day to keep the crisp short.

recipe_000144.title: Soufflé Cheese Tarts — fluffy cheese tartlets
recipe_000144.description: The Soufflé Cheese Tart combines shell of shorts already cooked with a light filling of cream cheese and mounted egg whites. The tarts are baked briefly until the surface is golden, preserving the soft center. The surface of the tarts is briefly gilded in the oven, leaving the center to the soft cheese instead of drying it excessively.
recipe_000144.animeContext: This recipe is thematically inspired by Food Wars!, Kaguya-sama: Love is War. These are editorial associations, not claims of appearances in specific episodes or chapters.

gusci_di_frolla_per_tartelletta_gia_cott.name: short shell for already cooked tartelletta

uovo.name: egg (separate egg yolks and egg whites)

stepTexts.step_1: Bring the stuffing ingredients to room temperature and prepare the already cooked and completely cold short shells.
stepTexts.step_2: Work cream cheese, butter, yolk, half the sugar, cream, starch and lemon juice until you get a smooth cream.
stepTexts.step_3: Add the remaining sugar gradually, stopping at a shiny meringue with soft peaks.
stepTexts.step_4: It incorporates the cream meringue in two shots, with delicate movements from the bottom to the top.
stepTexts.step_5: Fill the shells creating a small dome and smooth the surface.
stepTexts.step_6: Brush with little yolk or milk if you want a more intense gilding.
stepTexts.step_7: Bake at 200°C for about 10-12 minutes, until the surface is golden but the center remains soft.
stepTexts.step_8: Allow to warm a few minutes before serving, avoiding to cook them beyond the point where the filling loses creaminess.
